### The Region and the World
**Canada signs trade deal with UAE in push for non-US markets: Al Jazeera**
With a deal in Washington still out of reach, Canada and the United Arab Emirates said Tuesday they signed a comprehensive trade deal to lower barriers and boost investment. Prime Minister Mark Carney and Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan presided over the signing of the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement, which aims to cut tariffs, reduce red tape and improve market access. The Prime Minister's Office said that once fully implemented the pact will reduce or eliminate tariffs on over 99 percent of current Canadian exports to the UAE, opening markets the office named for pulses and canola, industrial machinery and power-generation equipment, aerospace and other innovators, and that CEPA is expected to enter into force in 2027. The office said the agreement will also address non-tariff barriers and expand access for goods and services in the industrial, agricultural, forest, fish and seafood, environmental and engineering sectors. The two governments also signed preliminary agreements on energy, diplomatic and defence cooperation. Foreign Trade Minister Thani bin Ahmed Al Zeyoudi, who signed with Canadian counterpart Maninder Sidhu, said the UAE sees potential for exporters and for investment in logistics, communications, advanced technology and manufacturing. Al Jazeera reported that the UAE is the largest Middle East market for Canadian exports and a major buyer of Canadian motor vehicles and parts and of machinery. Two-way trade was worth 3.5 billion Canadian dollars, about $2.48 billion, last year, and has been growing at 10 percent annually for the last few years, according to government data. The UAE committed up to $50 billion in investment in Canada last year. Carney has pledged to double Canada's non-U.S. trade over the next decade after President Donald Trump's tariffs rippled through the economy and later attempts to reach a deal with Washington broke down, pushing Ottawa toward pacts from the Asia Pacific to Europe and the Middle East. Source: [aljazeera.com](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/28/canada-signs-trade-deal-with-uae-in-push-for-non-us-markets) Source: [thediplomaticinsight.com](https://thediplomaticinsight.com/canada-uae-trade-deal-record-47-days/) Source: [thenationalnews.com](https://www.thenationalnews.com/news/uae/2026/10/28/sheikh-khaled-holds-talks-with-canadian-prime-minister-mark-carney-as-nations-boost-energy-and-investment-ties/)

# Omni View North America

> **A federal judge rejected Trump officials' bid to set aside California ballots, with no immediate action ordered.**

The New York Times describes the ruling as another setback as the administration moves to target voting by noncitizens. Ontario plans to appoint regional chairs within weeks, and American automakers say tariffs, diesel and computer chips are raising their costs.

### Lead
**Judge Rejects Trump Officials’ Bid to Set Aside California Ballots: The New York Times**
A federal judge rejected a bid by Trump officials to set aside California ballots. The judge ruled that no immediate action was necessary. The decision leaves the ballots in place for now, because the court found no immediate action was required. The administration's move, as The New York Times frames it, is aimed at voting by noncitizens. The ruling is a court result, not a new statute, and it answers the officials' request by declining to set the ballots aside. Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/28/us/politics/california-noncitizen-voters-trump.html)

### Across the Region
**Ontario will appoint hand-picked regional chairs within weeks. Critics call the move 'undemocratic': CBC**
CBC reports the appointments are coming on that timetable, with the chairs chosen by the province rather than left to voters. Critics call the move undemocratic. The criticism, as CBC presents it, is aimed at the method: hand-picked chairs, installed by appointment, on a clock measured in weeks. The step is an announcement of what the province will do, not a completed round of appointments already named in the report. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/lite/story/9.7398574)

**Tariffs, diesel and computer chips are driving up costs for automakers: NPR**
American auto companies say they are paying more for key components, naming computer chips, steel and copper, plus the fuel needed to transport their products. NPR reports tariffs, diesel and computer chips as what is driving those costs up. The companies' account covers both the parts that go into vehicles and the fuel that moves finished products. Tariffs sit in that list beside diesel and chips, as the companies and NPR describe the pressure on costs. The report is the companies' statement of higher bills, not a published price index. Source: [npr.org](https://www.npr.org/2026/10/29/nx-s1-6008066/automakers-inflation-tariffs-chips-diesel-earnings)

**Nvidia Chief, Jensen Huang, Is Seen as Target of Chinese Spy Plot: The New York Times**
The New York Times reports that Nvidia chief Jensen Huang is seen as the target of a Chinese spy plot. A Chinese businesswoman who had a close relationship with Huang was found to be passing intelligence to Beijing. President Trump was briefed and took no action. The finding, as the paper reports it, is that intelligence was passed to Beijing by someone close to Huang, and that the president, once briefed, did not act. The paper presents Huang as the person the plot is seen as targeting, and the businesswoman as the person found to be passing the intelligence. Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/29/us/politics/nvidia-china-jensen-huang-trump.html)

### The Closer Look
**Everybody hates Pat: is a cabal of college kids really trying to bring down ESPN’s star meathead?: The Guardian**
The Guardian reports that a handful of college students made jokes about Pat McAfee online ahead of his appearance with ESPN's College GameDay at the University of Utah. McAfee hosts The Pat McAfee Show. The Guardian says he landed a five-year, 85 million dollar deal in 2023 to take that show to ESPN, and that his persistently honking presence on College GameDay had helped push ratings to new heights. ESPN executives, the paper reports, were so impressed that they were reportedly in negotiations to award him a new contract worth between 60 million and 65 million dollars a year. One executive, The Guardian says, went so far as to describe him as a generational media talent. The outlet's own framing casts him as the star attraction of a bolder ESPN era of stunts, stupidity and what it calls memebrain swill. That is the paper's description, not a finding McAfee has adopted.

The Guardian says the weekend then went wrong, in the paper's telling. Students at Utah posted ahead of the GameDay appearance. The writer says "attacked" overstates it: they made a few mild jokes at his expense. McAfee's initial reaction, which The Guardian quotes, was mild. "The university's Instagram account posted something talking a little trash about me last night, which I certainly love," he said ahead of the Utes' clash with the Houston Cougars. The Guardian's argument, attributed to its writer, is that the reaction shows an ESPN personality happy to whip a crowd into a hostile frenzy but terrified of criticism. The piece does not report a cancelled appearance, a dropped contract or a ratings number for the Utah show. What it does report is the existing deal, the reported renewal range, the executive's "generational" description, the students' jokes, and McAfee's line about the university Instagram post before the Utes played Houston.

Who that touches is McAfee, the students who posted, ESPN's College GameDay set, and the Utah stop. The 85 million dollar, five-year deal dates to 2023. The reported talks, if the paper's account holds, would move him to between 60 million and 65 million dollars a year. The students' posts are what The Guardian says prompted the on-air remark. ESPN is the employer in both the 2023 deal and the reported negotiations. Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/oct/29/pat-mcafee-college-gameday-espn)

The government said in a court filing that it would meet the November 15 deadline set by President Trump to close East Potomac Park to build a championship golf course there. Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/28/us/politics/deadline-golf-course-closure.html)

**Five Takeaways From the New Hampshire Senate Debate: The New York Times**
In a New Hampshire Senate debate, Representative Chris Pappas and former Senator John E. Sununu both stressed a willingness to buck their parties on occasion, and neither had kind words for President Trump, The New York Times reports. Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/29/us/politics/pappas-sununu-new-hampshire-senate-debate.html)

**In Michigan, El-Sayed Faces Heat From Former Primary Rival as Election Nears: The New York Times**
Representative Haley Stevens has been less than enthusiastic about Dr. Abdul El-Sayed, injecting late intraparty tensions into a Michigan Senate race that could decide Senate control, The New York Times reports. Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/28/us/politics/stevens-el-sayed-senate-democrats-michigan.html)

**A Top Dartmouth Leader Steps Down Over Undisclosed A.I. Use in Writings: The New York Times**
Santiago Schnell, Dartmouth's provost since last year, will leave after a review found he had improperly used artificial intelligence in published opinion articles, The New York Times reports. Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/28/us/dartmouth-santiago-schnell-ai.html)

**Ahead of midterms, Missourians defend transgender healthcare: NPR**
The campaign to defend access to transgender healthcare for young people in Missouri is taking an unhurried approach to talking with voters about a proposed ban, NPR reports. Source: [npr.org](https://www.npr.org/2026/10/29/nx-s1-6017986/election-midterm-healthcare-transgender)

**Obama Campaigns in Georgia as Trump Rallies in Ohio: The New York Times**
Barack Obama is campaigning in Georgia as President Trump rallies in Ohio ahead of Election Day, The New York Times reports. Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/live/2026/10/28/us/midterms-elections-trump)

**Idaho Voters Will Pick Their State Gun on Tuesday: The New York Times**
An advisory referendum will give Idahoans a choice of six weapons to make their state gun, though none of them are exactly linked to their state, The New York Times reports. Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/29/us/elections/idaho-state-gun-referendum.html)

**Brewers beat the Rays to win the first World Series title in franchise history: NPR**
The Milwaukee Brewers beat the Rays to win the first World Series title in franchise history, in the 58th season of a club that began as the Seattle Pilots in 1969, NPR reports. Source: [npr.org](https://www.npr.org/2026/10/29/nx-s1-6021953/brewers-win-first-world-series-title)

The European Union has backtracked on Canada becoming an associate member, Al Jazeera reports. The two accounts sit together: Ottawa is receiving European leaders while the associate-member label, as Al Jazeera puts it, is no longer where the European Union had put it. The resistance the Seattle Times names is to the membership label itself, not to the meetings Carney is hosting. The push the Seattle Times attributes to President Trump is what it says is moving Canada toward Europe. Source: [aljazeera.com](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/29/european-union-backtracks-on-canada-becoming-associate-2) Source: [seattletimes.com](https://www.seattletimes.com/business/carney-hosts-eu-leaders-as-trump-pushes-canada-toward-europe-but-membership-label-faces-resistance/)

episodes.content:
# Omni View North America
> **More than fifteen thousand veterans pay a thousand dollars more each month after VA cut a loan program.**

NPR’s investigation finds those military veterans were put into much-higher-cost home loans after the Trump administration ended the program. Bayer won a Roundup cancer trial involving three women, Quebec’s premier is skipping the Canada-EU summit in Montreal, and cartel roadblocks have closed the bridges between Brownsville and Matamoros.

### Lead
**Trump's VA killed a home loan program. Thousands of veterans are paying the price: NPR**
NPR reports that the Trump administration cut a key home-loan program at the Department of Veterans Affairs. An NPR investigation finds that more than 15,000 military veterans were put into much-higher-cost home loans after that cut. Many of those veterans now pay $1,000 more per month. NPR presents the higher monthly bills as the price those veterans are paying. The count of veterans and the extra monthly cost both come from that investigation. The loans in question are home loans, and the department whose program was cut is Veterans Affairs. Source: [npr.org](https://www.npr.org/2026/10/30/nx-s1-5995628/trump-va-home-loan-program-veterans-paying)

### Across the Region
**Bayer wins Roundup weedkiller cancer trial while awaiting settlement ruling: Reuters**
Bayer has won a United States trial over claims that its Roundup weedkiller caused cancer in three women, Reuters reports. Seeking Alpha reports the same result and says it is Bayer’s first such victory since the Supreme Court ruled in the company’s favor in June. The claims in the trial concerned three women. Reuters reports that the company is still awaiting a settlement ruling. The result the two outlets report is a win in that trial. Neither outlet states a broader finding on Roundup beyond the verdict and the settlement ruling still ahead. Source: [reuters.com](https://www.reuters.com/world/bayer-wins-us-trial-which-it-was-alleged-that-roundup-caused-cancer-three-women-2026-10-30/) Source: [seekingalpha.com](https://seekingalpha.com/news/4661181-bayer-wins-first-roundup-trial-after-supreme-court-ruling)

**Quebec Premier skips Canada-EU summit in Montreal over Ottawa’s refusal to let him speak: The Globe and Mail**
Quebec’s premier is skipping the Canada-European Union summit in Montreal over Ottawa’s refusal to let him speak, The Globe and Mail reports. The Globe and Mail calls that absence the first move in what it describes as a combative relationship with the federal government. Prime Minister Mark Carney is hosting European Union leaders in Montreal on Friday, CBC reports. CBC says he is looking to deepen ties with like-minded leaders in the face of an increasingly protectionist United States. Carney points to the European Union’s strong belief in democracy as political winds shift for the bloc’s two largest members, CBC reports. CBC says the rise of nationalist political forces in Europe could make that deepening more difficult in the years to come. Source: [theglobeandmail.com](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/canada/article-quebec-st-pierre-plamondon-canada-eu-summit-montreal-ottawa/) Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/european-union-canada-associate-member-von-der-leyen-9.7401989?cmp=rss)

**Cartel roadblocks paralyze Matamoros after arrest of Gulf Cartel leader’s son: Mexico News Daily**
The security incident triggered the temporary closure of the international bridges between Brownsville, Texas, and Matamoros. Those bridges are a United States-Mexico crossing, so the closure lands on traffic between the two countries. Source: [mexiconewsdaily.com](https://mexiconewsdaily.com/news/cartel-roadblocks-matamoros-arrest-gulf-cartel-leader-son/)

### The Closer Look
**Quebec farmers say proposed high-speed rail threatens their land, livelihoods: Global News**
Farmers and local elected officials in Repentigny, Quebec, are calling for a proposed high-speed rail project to be scrapped. They fear the line could cut through agricultural land and threaten their livelihoods. Guillaume Alary, a third-generation crop farmer, told Global News on Thursday that he fears the proposed rail line could divide his property and fundamentally change the life his family has built there. He said he is concerned about his land, his family, and the land and families of his neighbours. Alary owns more than 260 hectares, where he grows wheat, corn and soybeans and produces hay. His family’s farming history on the property dates back to his grandfather. He said he is left wondering how much of that land he could lose, and he asked whether he will lose half his land or his house. He said he learned about the project at the beginning of the year but was never consulted, and that he is upset about a project that is not transparent.

Alto, the federal agency overseeing the project, is proposing a high-speed rail network between Quebec City and Toronto. Much of the proposed route is mapped along agricultural property. Simon Duval, regional president of the Union des producteurs agricoles in Lanaudière, said that what farmers have to do right now is stop the project. He said that if half a farm ends up on the other side of the line, the detour required to reach it is going to totally ruin the financial aspect of the operation. In a statement to Global News, an Alto spokesperson said the agency held consultations earlier this year and received 20,000 comments. The spokesperson said that as the corridor approaches more urbanized areas such as Repentigny, the priority is to identify a route that minimizes impacts on residential neighbourhoods and agricultural lands.

Bloc Québécois MP Patrick Bonin, who represents Repentigny, said he cannot support the project. He said there is no proper public consultation and environmental assessment. Repentigny city councillor Normand Urbain raised the question of moving equipment. He asked listeners to imagine a train passing in the middle of farmland, and said a farmer cannot bring tractors from one side to the other because the farmer cannot pass over the rails. For Alary, the uncertainty reaches a way of life passed down through generations. He said he would be losing a piece of his reason to live. Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12126696/quebec-farmers-high-speed-rail-alto/)

### Also Today
**Over 5,200 U.S. troops heading to Mexico border: Reuters**
Reuters reports that more than 5,200 United States troops are heading to the Mexico border. Source: [reuters.com](https://www.reuters.com/video/watch/idOV944KP9B/)

**Homeland Security Leak Exposes More Than 41,000 Employees: The New York Times**
A nonprofit said it released information on more than 41,000 Homeland Security employees to promote transparency about the Trump administration’s deportation campaign, and homeland security officials told workers they are reviewing the incident, The New York Times reports. Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/29/us/politics/homeland-security-hack.html)

**Trump Administration Pressures California With Expanded Voter Fraud Investigation: The New York Times**
The Justice Department has issued grand jury subpoenas to local election officials in California as part of a widening effort to prove claims about large numbers of illegal voters, claims The New York Times describes as unsubstantiated. Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/29/us/trump-doj-california-voter-rolls-midterms.html)

**Georgia Republican Donor Gets 15 Years in $76 Million Ponzi Scheme: The New York Times**
A federal court sentenced Edwin Brant Frost IV to 15 years in a $76 million Ponzi scheme, and federal prosecutors said he lured investors with promises of high returns but used new money to pay earlier investors and fund personal expenses. Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/29/us/politics/edwin-frost-georgia-ponzi-scheme-sentencing.html)

**Canada investing $1.6 billion in AI firm Cohere: Carney: Canadian Affairs**
Prime Minister Mark Carney says Canada is investing $1.6 billion in the artificial-intelligence firm Cohere. Source: [canadianaffairs.news](https://www.canadianaffairs.news/2026/10/30/canada-investing-1-6-billion-in-ai-firm-cohere-carney/)

**Winnipeg voters return Gillingham to mayor’s office as challengers struggle to capture public interest: The Globe and Mail**
Winnipeg voters returned Mayor Gillingham to office with just under 40 percent of the vote, according to unofficial results, and he acknowledged that slender mandate, The Globe and Mail reports. Source: [theglobeandmail.com](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/canada/article-winnipeg-voters-return-gillingham-to-mayors-office-as-challengers/)

**Three members of family shot, another injured in Bridle Path home invasion: The Globe and Mail**
Toronto police say masked attackers entered a Bridle Path home around 3 a.m., shot three members of a family, injured another, and demanded “nice things,” The Globe and Mail reports. Source: [theglobeandmail.com](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/canada/toronto/article-toronto-bridle-path-home-invasion/)

**El-Sayed and Stevens to make rare joint appearance as Democrats seek unity in Michigan Senate race: AP News**
Dr. Abdul El-Sayed and Representative Haley Stevens are set to make a rare joint appearance as Democrats seek unity in Michigan’s Senate race, AP News reports. Source: [apnews.com](https://apnews.com/article/michigan-senate-abdul-elsayed-mike-rogers-bc0c09058cb388f0a64a82a5c53520a9)

**Summerland landslides raise concerns after wildfire leaves slopes vulnerable: Global News**
Heavy rain on Tuesday triggered landslides in Summerland, with debris spilling into a field on a family’s property, after a wildfire left the slopes vulnerable, Global News reports. Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12126734/summerland-landslides-concerns-wildfire-slopes-vulnerable/)

**Nearly 2 out of 3 teens and tweens use AI chatbots, new research shows: NPR**
New research reported by NPR finds that nearly two out of three teens and tweens use AI chatbots, most often for homework and when they are stressed, lonely, or anxious, and that how they use the chatbots is tied to their mental health. Source: [npr.org](https://www.npr.org/2026/10/30/nx-s1-6022278/ai-artificial-intelligence-teens-jed-common-sense-media)

**Democrats seek to weaken the Republican lead in state legislatures: NPR**
Republicans control 10 more state legislatures than Democrats, NPR reports, and Democrats are seeking to weaken that lead in chambers where most laws on taxes, abortion, crime and schools are made. Source: [npr.org](https://www.npr.org/2026/10/30/nx-s1-6022353/midterms-state-legislatures-pennsylvania)

**Pennsylvania’s Legislature Is Losing Its Climate Champion: Inside Climate News**
Inside Climate News reports that Pennsylvania’s legislature is losing its climate champion, Greg Vitali. Source: [insideclimatenews.org](https://insideclimatenews.org/news/30102026/pennsylvania-legislature-loses-climate-champion-greg-vitali/)

### The Region and the World
**Loss of Canadian shoppers a $64M hit to Washington State: report: Global News**
A report cited by Global News puts the loss of Canadian shoppers at a $64 million hit to Washington State. Canadian shopping visits have dropped 71 percent compared with 2019. The report says that drop is largely driven by the strained political and economic climate between the two countries and a weak Canadian dollar. The missing trips are spending Washington retailers are not receiving. Global News is the outlet carrying the report’s figures on the American side of that cross-border shopping. Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12126741/washington-state-canadian-shoppers-report/)

The day had no measured improvement to report.

episodes.content:
# Omni View North America

> **Four hundred ninety-five million dollars bought a Minnesota immigrant prison the state refused at seventy-five million.**

**What You Need to Know:** The Department of Homeland Security paid $495 million for a Minnesota prison the state had declined to buy for $75 million, to hold immigrants. A federal judge has barred the Trump administration from threatening to prosecute election workers in California. Elections Alberta has asked legislators to hold a new riding map or postpone the 2027 vote.

### Lead
**Minnesota Declined to Buy a Prison for $75 Million. D.H.S. Paid $495 Million.: The New York Times**
The Department of Homeland Security paid $495 million for a prison in Minnesota that the state had declined to buy for $75 million, The New York Times reports. The purchase is to hold immigrants. The Times reports the deal is among acquisitions facing scrutiny in the Trump administration’s mass deportation push. Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/30/us/minnesota-prison-homeland-security.html)

### Across the Region
**Judge Bars Trump Administration From Threatening to Prosecute Election Workers in California: The New York Times**
A judge has barred the Trump administration from threatening to prosecute election workers in California, The New York Times reports. The Times reports the ruling could deprive the Justice Department of its most important leverage in extracting concessions from local officials, the threat of prosecution. The order limits that threat; the article does not describe a completed prosecution. Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/30/us/elections/california-unions-lawsuit-justice-department-election-immigrants.html)

**Elections Alberta urges MLAs to hold off on approving new electoral map or postpone 2027 vote: The Globe and Mail**
Elections Alberta has urged members of the legislative assembly to hold off on approving a new electoral map or to postpone the 2027 vote, The Globe and Mail reports. In a letter to MLAs, the agency says it lacks the resources to implement new riding boundaries before the election. The letter is a request to legislators, not a change already made to the map or the date. Source: [theglobeandmail.com](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/canada/alberta/article-elections-alberta-urges-mlas-to-hold-off-on-approving-new-electoral/)

**Plans for a data center threaten scenic wilderness and dark skies in West Virginia: NPR**
Residents in West Virginia are fighting plans for a data-center project that would span thousands of acres near the Monongahela National Forest, NPR reports. The land in question is also near popular outdoor recreation, ski areas, and dark-sky sites. The dispute is over that footprint, not over a project NPR describes as already built. Source: [npr.org](https://www.npr.org/2026/10/31/nx-s1-5992790/data-centers-west-virginia-skiing-dark-skies)

### The Closer Look
**How fraudsters got a slice of Canada’s bread price-fixing settlement: The Globe and Mail**
After Canada’s bread price-fixing payments went out in May, a market in forwarded e-transfer links appeared, and one bank customer deposited roughly 1,000 of those transfers into a single account, The Globe and Mail reports. Loblaw Cos. Ltd. and its parent, George Weston Ltd., had agreed to pay $500 million for their role in a scheme to fix bread prices. For most recipients the sum was $49.11, sent as an Interac e-transfer. Ken Wu, a Vancouver resident, told the Globe that a stranger on the Chinese app RedNote contacted him this past spring with a split: the stranger had registered with different email addresses, the links could be forwarded, and anyone with a Canadian bank account who opened them could deposit the money, after an upfront payment priced below the payout. Wu, a newcomer who had not bought bread at Loblaw stores in the period covered by the lawsuit, refused that offer and others. He said, “I don’t have that right.” Once people began posting that payments had arrived, the Globe reports, comments on RedNote filled with offers of links, some on generous terms for anyone willing to make, in some cases, hundreds of deposits. The paper says it is impossible to know how many of those posts sold working links and how many looked for someone who would pay and get nothing.

The settlement was the first to emerge from lawsuits launched after the companies reported an alleged industry-wide conspiracy to the Competition Bureau in 2015, in exchange for immunity from criminal prosecution. Other grocers have denied involvement. Canadians who bought bread between 2001 and 2021 were eligible. Court documents last year listed Avocats Inc. among administrators hired by the lawyers and responsible for security procedures meant to prevent fraud. Concilia Services Inc. was chosen by the settlement administrators to make the payments. Loblaw and George Weston worked with those administrators so the payments could be made.

Three small institutions then reported unusual account activity to the settlement administrator, Verita Global LLC, and to its banking partner, the Bank of Nova Scotia. Multiple bread payments were being funnelled into the same accounts, including the customer who deposited roughly 1,000 e-transfers. The Globe reports that when fake claims succeed, legitimate claimants receive a smaller share, and that official estimates of suspicious deposits into Canadian banks have grown. Many applications to the publicized fund, the paper says, were bogus. Source: [theglobeandmail.com](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/canada/article-loblaw-bread-price-fixing-settlement-payout-fraud-class-action-lawsuit/)

### Also Today
**Judge Blocks Expediting Migrant Children’s Asylum Cases, For Now: The New York Times**
A judge has blocked, for now, the fast-tracking of asylum interviews for unaccompanied migrant children, and lawyers for the children called the pause a blow against what they termed the Trump administration’s “deportation assembly line,” The New York Times reports. Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/30/us/politics/children-asylum-fast-track-deport.html)

**Despite concerns, the Trump administration still sends pregnant migrant minors to south Texas: NPR**
NPR reports the Trump administration is still sending pregnant migrant minors to south Texas, and that several children have had to leave the state for medical care, including abortions, that is unavailable in Texas. Source: [npr.org](https://www.npr.org/2026/10/30/nx-s1-6022578/minors-pregnant-migrant-texas-trump)

**US court lifts ruling requiring Idaho to allow some abortions to protect women's health: Reuters**
A U.S. court has lifted a ruling that required Idaho to allow some abortions to protect women’s health, Reuters reports. Source: [reuters.com](https://www.reuters.com/legal/government/us-court-lifts-ruling-requiring-idaho-allow-some-abortions-protect-womens-health-2026-10-30/)

**After last year's storm, this remote Alaska town is still picking up the pieces: NPR**
NPR reports that remnants of a typhoon in October 2025 seriously damaged Alaska Native villages in far western Alaska, and that a year later one of the hardest-hit communities is still recovering. Source: [npr.org](https://www.npr.org/2026/10/31/nx-s1-6021471/ex-typhoon-halong-damages-western-alaska-native-villages-kipnuk)

**He was one of the NFL’s most feared runners. Now Larry Johnson fears what football did to his brain: The Guardian**
Larry Johnson, 46, a former Kansas City Chiefs All-Pro who left the N.F.L. in 2011 after seven seasons, tells The Guardian he can recall his career only up to about 2006 or 2007, and not the years before that or the three years after, and that he fears what football did to his brain. Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/oct/31/larry-johnson-nfl-cte-brain-injuries-kansas-city-chiefs)

**Saturday is last day of early voting — and last chance to register to vote in NC: WRAL**
WRAL reports that Saturday is the last day of early voting in North Carolina and the last chance to register to vote there. Source: [wral.com](https://www.wral.com/news/nccapitol/end-early-voting-nc-last-day-register-how-to-guide-midterms-mail-id-2026/)

**Idaho Supreme Court upholds dismissal of legal challenge to state public defense office: Bonner County Daily Bee**
The Idaho Supreme Court has upheld the dismissal of a legal challenge to the state’s public defense office, the Bonner County Daily Bee reports. Source: [bonnercountydailybee.com](https://bonnercountydailybee.com/news/2026/oct/31/idaho-supreme-court-upholds-dismissal-of-legal-challenge-to-state-public-defense-office/)

**B.C.’s non-time change could impact technology and travel: Global News**
Global News reports that British Columbia’s shift this weekend to permanent Pacific daylight time could affect technology and travel, not only the missed extra hour of sleep. Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12128115/bc-non-time-change-impact-technology-travel/)

**Eviction day at contentious homeless encampment in Penticton: Global News**
On eviction day at a homeless encampment in Penticton, Global News reports, R.C.M.P. officers were on scene and outreach workers helped roughly a dozen residents vacate the property. Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12128169/eviction-day-contentious-homeless-encampment-penticton/)

**Alberta cutting education portion of property taxes in province: CityNews Calgary**
CityNews Calgary reports that Alberta is cutting the education portion of property taxes in the province. Source: [calgary.citynews.ca](https://calgary.citynews.ca/2026/10/30/alberta-cutting-education-portion-of-property-taxes-in-province/)

**Repercussions of Alberta referendum’s immigration question ripple through UCP, province: The Globe and Mail**
The Globe and Mail reports that some of Premier Danielle Smith’s former backers are abandoning her, and that business groups are raising the alarm about the province turning against immigration, as repercussions of an immigration question on an Alberta referendum move through the United Conservative Party and the province. Source: [theglobeandmail.com](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/canada/alberta/article-repercussions-alberta-referendum-immigration-question-ucp-danielle/)

**Decision clearing path for Russia to join world juniors in Alberta is 'very unwelcome,' minister says: CBC**
Canada’s foreign affairs minister called a decision clearing the way for Russia to join the world junior hockey championships in Alberta “very unwelcome” and a “great disappointment,” and said Canada is exploring options, CBC reports, as Russia’s invasion of Ukraine stretches toward its fifth year. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/russia-hockey-world-junior-championships-2027-canada-exploring-options-minister-says-9.7403796?cmp=rss)

**Ontario is projecting a larger deficit than expected. Here's what that could mean: CBC**
CBC reports that Ontario is projecting a larger deficit than expected. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/toronto/ontario-larger-deficit-projection-reaction-9.7403840)

**PQ appoints political commentator as chief of staff to government efficiency minister: CBC**
CBC reports that the Parti Québécois has appointed a political commentator as chief of staff to the government efficiency minister. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/montreal/jacinthe-eve-arel-9.7403444)

**Trump should 'take stock' and 'own' election outcome, Sen. Tillis says: PBS**
PBS reports that Senator Tillis says President Trump should take stock and own the election outcome. Source: [pbs.org](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/show/trump-should-take-stock-and-own-election-outcome-sen-tillis-says)

### The Region and the World
**Carney eyes June deal for Canada to become EU associate member as Trump reshapes alliances: AP News**
Prime Minister Mark Carney is eyeing a June deal for Canada to become an associate member of the European Union, the Associated Press reports, as President Trump reshapes alliances. The Canadian Broadcasting Corporation reports that Carney has confirmed Canada’s European Union ambitions. The June date is a target he is pursuing, not an agreement already signed. For Canada, the two reports put an associate-member deal on a June calendar while Washington’s alliances are shifting. Source: [apnews.com](https://apnews.com/article/canada-eu-carney-trump-d8543b3d496dd2b98d68b4ca13e7f2f8) Source: [cbc.ca](http://www.cbc.ca/player/play/video/9.7404089)

The day had no measured improvement to report.

episodes.episode_title: Ep 34: Ten billion dollars is out of Trump's Journal case after a judge barred any refiling.
episodes.content:
# Omni View North America
> **Ten billion dollars is out of Trump's Journal case after a judge barred any refiling.**

**What You Need to Know:** A federal judge has thrown out President Donald Trump's ten-billion-dollar defamation lawsuit against the Wall Street Journal and Rupert Murdoch, and barred him from filing it again. Judge Darrin Gayles found Trump had not shown actual malice over a July 2025 report about an alleged 2003 letter to Jeffrey Epstein. Trump denies wrongdoing and has not been charged.

### Lead
**'Grasping at straws': Judge dismisses Trump suit against Wall Street Journal over Epstein letter: NPR**
A US judge on Saturday dismissed President Donald Trump's defamation lawsuit against the Wall Street Journal and media magnate Rupert Murdoch over a report on his ties to Jeffrey Epstein. Trump had sued for 10 billion dollars after the newspaper's story was published in July 2025 detailing the president's alleged 2003 letter to Epstein, which apparently featured a drawing of a naked woman. In Saturday's ruling, Judge Darrin Gayles dismissed the lawsuit with prejudice, meaning Trump cannot file an amended version of the suit, as he did when Gayles turned down an initial version of it back in April. The judge wrote that in bringing his defamation claim, Trump had both times failed to establish that the defendants "acted with actual malice." NPR reported that the judge, saying the president was "grasping at straws," threw the case out. Murdoch is the founder of News Corp., which owns the Wall Street Journal. The House Oversight Committee last year published a copy of Trump's alleged birthday note to Epstein, a short dialogue between "Donald" and "Jeffrey": Donald says, "We have certain things in common," Jeffrey answers, "Yes, we do, come to think of it," Donald asks, "Enigmas never age, have you noticed that?" Jeffrey says, "As a matter of fact, it was clear to me the last time I saw you," and the note ends, "A pal is a wonderful thing. Happy Birthday — and may every day be another wonderful secret," followed by Trump's signature, which takes the place of pubic hair on the nude outline. Channels Television reported that the story piled scrutiny on Trump from Democrats and from his own Republican party, who rejected the president's attempts to downplay the saga as a hoax and called for a full release of legal files on Epstein. Trump's name appears repeatedly in the documents, but he denies any wrongdoing and has not been charged with any criminal offenses connected to the affair. The president fought for months to prevent the Department of Justice from releasing the so-called "Epstein Files" but eventually signed a law passed by Congress requiring their publication. Ahead of the November 3 US midterm elections, which will decide control of Congress, Democrats have reportedly spent more than 35 million dollars on Epstein-related advertisements. With a Republican majority in the House and Senate, Trump has so far enjoyed relatively little political opposition since taking office in January 2025, giving the courts a key role in limiting him. Source: [npr.org](https://www.npr.org/2026/11/01/nx-s1-6025342/judge-dismisses-trump-suit-against-wall-street-journal-epstein-letter) Source: [channelstv.com](https://www.channelstv.com/2026/11/01/us-judge-dismisses-trump-lawsuit-against-wall-street-journal-over-epstein-letter/)

> **Nine people died when a business jet nosedived into a South Florida neighborhood.**

**What You Need to Know:** Nine people died when a business jet nosedived into a South Florida neighborhood on Sunday, after a pilot reported a descent of twenty thousand feet a minute. New York Times/Siena polls find Democrats ahead or tied across a run of Senate and governor races the day before the midterms. In Canada, a senior government source says Prime Minister Mark Carney’s second budget, due Thursday, will carry affordability measures and business tax incentives.

### Lead
**Learjet Plummets to Ground in Florida, Killing 9: The New York Times**
A business jet hit a South Florida neighborhood on Sunday, exploded into a fireball, and killed everyone on board. The New York Times reported that photos and video posted online showed the jet diving nose first to the ground and exploding. In a radio call, a pilot said the plane was descending at twenty thousand feet per minute. A second Times account called the aircraft a midsize jet and said it plummeted on Sunday, exploding into a fireball and killing all on board. The Times headlines identify the jet as a Learjet. NPR reported that Transportation Secretary Duffy said all nine people aboard died. Duffy, in that account, said the business jet crashed into a Florida neighborhood. The aircraft had departed Austin, Texas, and was headed to the Bahamas. NPR placed the crash near a busy roadway. The death toll both newsrooms report is nine, and both describe the impact as a fireball or an explosion after a nose-first dive. Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/01/us/florida-plane-crash-palm-beach-county.html) Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/01/us/learjet-crash-florida-palm-beach.html) Source: [npr.org](https://www.npr.org/2026/11/02/g-s1-151211/south-florida-jet-crash)

### Across the Region
**Canada's next budget to be unveiled this week amid U.S. trade war, economic uncertainty: CBC**
Prime Minister Mark Carney’s second budget is set to be unveiled on Thursday. A senior government source told CBC the budget will include new affordability measures. The same source said it will include business tax incentives. The source also said it will include investments in infrastructure, defence, and culture. CBC set that preview against the U.S. trade war and economic uncertainty. What the source described is the planned contents of a budget still to be unveiled, not a text Parliament has passed. Thursday is the date CBC gives for the unveiling. The measures named are affordability, business tax incentives, infrastructure, defence, and culture, each attributed to that senior government source rather than to a published budget document. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/budget-carney-affordability-investments-9.7404193?cmp=rss) Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/budget-carney-affordability-investments-9.7404193)

**El-Sayed's primary opponent stuns Democrats by endorsing Republican opponent in Michigan Senate race: AP News**
Democratic Representative Haley Stevens, Abdul El-Sayed’s primary opponent, has endorsed the Republican in Michigan’s Senate race. The Associated Press said the endorsement stunned Democrats. A New York Times headline said Democrats fume after the defeated Senate candidate backed the Republican rival. NPR’s morning brief reported the same endorsement, identifying Stevens as the Democrat who endorsed the Republican candidate in the Michigan race. That brief said key races remain close on the last day before the midterm election. The Associated Press framed the move as a break in Democratic unity in the Michigan contest. Neither account names the Republican candidate in the lines provided. The endorsement lands on the final day before voters cast midterm ballots, which is the timing NPR gives. Source: [apnews.com](https://apnews.com/article/elsayed-michigan-stevens-democrats-unity-midterms-d7053bbd0ed2fd70756896c6e4b66a27) Source: [npr.org](https://www.npr.org/2026/11/02/nx-s1-6023084/morning-news-brief) Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/live/2026/11/01/us/midterms-elections-trump)

**Democrats Show Strength in Final Days of Race for the Senate, New Polls Find: The New York Times**
New York Times/Siena polls found Democrats up in Michigan, Texas, Kansas, Maine, and Ohio. The same polls found Democrats with an edge in Alaska. They found Democrats effectively tied with Republicans in Iowa. A companion Times/Siena survey found Democrats leading or tied in seven battleground governor’s races. The Times said those governor findings underscore how a favorable political environment may be lifting Democrats, which is the paper’s reading of its own polls. Polling reporter Ruth Igielnik said Democrats have the lead in most of seven tossup Senate races, though some contests remain close. The Times said the country is one day away from the midterms. These are poll findings, not results, and no outcome is settled by them. Nate Cohn, the Times chief political analyst, said polls show some kind of wave seems likely for the Democrats, and he outlined four possible scenarios for whether that would flip the House and the Senate. The paper’s separate account of closing arguments said Republicans, worried about losing control of Congress, are sending dire warnings about the opposing party, while Democrats are trying to keep their focus on affordability, corruption, and President Trump. Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/01/us/politics/times-siena-poll-senate.html) Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/01/us/politics/times-siena-poll-governor.html) Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/video/us/elections/100000011241496/whos-winning-the-race-for-the-senate.html) Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/02/us/politics/congress-races-midterms.html) Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/video/us/elections/100000011228691/what-a-blue-wave-could-look-like.html) Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/02/us/politics/midterm-elections.html)

episodes.episode_title: Ep 36: Four hundred thirty-five House seats are on the ballot as voters decide Congress.
episodes.content:
# Omni View North America
> **Four hundred thirty-five House seats are on the ballot as voters decide Congress.**

**What You Need to Know:** Voters across the United States began casting ballots Tuesday in midterms that decide which party controls Congress for the last two years of President Trump’s second term. All 435 House seats are up, and Democrats need a net gain of four to take the chamber from a narrow Republican majority. Thirty-five Senate seats are up as well; Republicans hold 53 seats, and Democrats need four gains while holding their own.

### Lead
**Voters head to the polls as control of Congress is on the ballot: The New York Times**
Voters across the United States began heading to the polls on Tuesday in midterms that will decide which party controls Congress for the final two years of President Trump’s second term, the New York Times and The Guardian report. All 435 voting House seats are contested; The Guardian reports Republicans are defending a narrow majority and Democrats need a net gain of four seats to take the House. Thirty-five Senate seats are up — 33 in regular elections and special elections in Florida and Ohio — and Republicans hold 53 seats against 47 held by Democrats and independents who caucus with them; The Guardian reports Democrats need to gain four seats and defend all of their own to secure a majority. NBC News reports Democrats would have to flip at least two states President Trump won by double digits in 2024. Voters are also choosing governors in 36 states and three US territories, 39 governorships in all, plus thousands of state legislative seats, local offices, judicial contests and ballot measures on taxes, abortion rights and voting rules. The New York Times reports Mr. Trump has urged supporters to act as if he is on the ballot and has insisted Republicans would win if his base turned out; Democratic campaigns have blamed the president and his signature policies for household struggles; Republicans have tried to turn the election into a choice against opponents they cast as radical, far-left activists. The Times reports this is the most expensive midterm in political advertising since at least 2018, according to AdImpact, and that Elon Musk contributed $474 million to Republican candidates and their allies. The first polls close at 7 p.m. Eastern; the Times says full results could take days or weeks, and that in 2024 it took three weeks to determine winners in California’s closest House races. A federal judge turned down a request by Democratic lawmakers and party organizations to prohibit the Trump administration from coercing states into screening incoming ballots, and the Supreme Court signaled it was not interested in assisting Mr. Trump’s efforts to interfere with how states administer elections, the Times reports. The Guardian reports the president’s party has lost House seats in 18 of the past 20 midterms, a stretch back to 1946. Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/live/2026/11/03/us/midterms-2026-election-day-trump/heres-the-latest) Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/live/2026/nov/03/midterm-elections-live-updates-voting) Source: [nbcnews.com](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-elections/senate-results)

### Across the Region
**How a New Brunswick island is caught in the middle of the Canada-U.S. trade war: Global News**
About 900 people live on Campobello Island, New Brunswick, whose only road bridge runs to Lubec, Maine, not to the rest of Canada, Global News reports. There is no gas station on the island and grocery options are limited, so residents cross for basic goods; a student who lives on the island and attends high school in the United States said she crosses the border almost every morning. Residents paid a 25 per cent tariff on US goods brought across the border until Ottawa announced a special exemption for the island. Last month a truckload of supplies was turned back by US border officials, and a Campobello brewery has shut down because of the tariffs. Canadian tourism to Maine was cut in half last year following President Trump’s taunts and tariffs. New Brunswick MP John Williamson said decisions made in distant capitals hit Campobello immediately; Lubec resident Nelson Meaker said there is no reason to cause bad blood among good neighbours. American fisherman Dana Barker, who has lived on the island with his Canadian wife for 50 years, said the two sides will work it out. Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12130717/island-caught-canada-u-s-tensions-midterms-campobello-nb/)

**Maine Senate pits Susan Collins against Troy Jackson: PBS**
Maine’s Senate election pits incumbent Republican Senator Susan Collins against Democrat Troy Jackson, a former state Senate president, PBS reports. Collins, first elected in 1996, is seeking a sixth term; PBS reports she is the only Republican senator from a state Vice President Kamala Harris won in the 2024 presidential election, and that she won by nine points in 2020 when polls showed her losing. Oyster farmer Graham Platner won the Democratic primary by a landslide in June, then dropped out a month later after sexual assault allegations emerged. A party convention then chose Jackson, a former logger whose campaign has centered on working-class economics. Source: [pbs.org](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/live-results-maine-senate-midterm-election)

**Ukrainian truckers who fled war swept up in immigration stops: The New York Times**
At least a dozen Ukrainian truck drivers were arrested this summer, according to a representative for Ukraine, and several remain in detention, the New York Times reports. On Monday, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said officers across 15 states had stopped more than 1,000 commercial trucks and arrested about 40 immigrant drivers, including some with serious criminal charges. Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/03/us/ukraine-immigrant-trucker-cdl-weigh-stations-ice.html)

### The Closer Look
**Ohio’s Senate, governor and House races on a right-shifted map: PBS**
Voters in Ohio are choosing a US senator in a special election, a governor, and the state’s 15 US House seats on Tuesday, in a state the Associated Press, via PBS, describes as having shifted sharply toward the right over the last decade. Polls close at 7:30 p.m. Eastern. For Democrats nationally, PBS reports, Ohio may be crucial to a bid to retake Congress.

Republican Jon Husted faces Democrat Sherrod Brown for the Senate seat. Husted was appointed in 2025 by Republican Governor Mike DeWine to fill the vacancy JD Vance left when he became vice president. The winner serves the remaining two years of that term. Brown held Ohio’s other Senate seat for three terms until 2025, when Republican Bernie Moreno defeated him in a tight race. President Trump carried Ohio in the last three presidential elections, and Republicans have controlled the governor’s office and the state Legislature for more than a decade. Husted has the president’s endorsement.

The cost of living has been a core issue. Brown has tied Trump’s war in Iran to climbing gas prices and attacked Husted for repeated votes against war-powers resolutions that could have directed the president to end the conflict. In September, Husted said the war needs to come to an end as quickly as possible so gas prices can be lowered. Brown has labeled Husted “the face of data centers,” a reference to Husted’s support for data-center projects as lieutenant governor, a post he held until 2025. In August, the National Republican Senatorial Committee warned in a memo that Husted could lose because of data centers.

Brown raised over $68.4 million as of mid-October, against $19.9 million raised by Husted. Hundreds of millions of dollars more have been spent by outside groups to oppose both campaigns.

DeWine cannot run for reelection because of term limits. Democrat Amy Acton, a physician, faces Republican Vivek Ramaswamy, a billionaire biotech entrepreneur and Trump ally. Acton was Ohio’s public-health director, a post DeWine appointed her to early in the pandemic; she implemented strict public-health measures that prompted a backlash. In the weeks before the election, Ramaswamy defended his campaign’s decision to publish an ad in which Acton’s estranged mother calls Acton a “liar.” Acton was removed from her mother’s custody at 12 after her stepfather was indicted for raping her. Trump has stood by Ramaswamy since the ad made national news. DeWine called for the ad to be taken down. On Thursday, Ramaswamy said the ad’s planned run was over.

Certain House races became more competitive after mid-decade redistricting favoring Republicans. In the 9th District, Democratic Representative Marcy Kaptur, who has held the seat since 1983, faces a rematch with Republican Derek Merrin, a former state House member. In 2024, before that redistricting, Kaptur won by less than one percentage point. In the 7th District, Republican Representative Max Miller faces Brian Poindexter, a union organizer and ironworker. Miller’s ex-wife, Emily Moreno, alleged that Miller abused her. Her father, Senator Bernie Moreno, and Husted have called on Miller to drop out. episodes.episode_title: Ep 37: Democrats won both the House and the Senate, ending Republican control of Congress.
episodes.content:
# Omni View North America

> **Democrats won both the House and the Senate, ending Republican control of Congress.**

**What You Need to Know:** Democrats won both the House and the Senate, ending Republican control of Congress and, as The New York Times reported, the party's hold on the House, the Senate and the presidency together. President Trump attributed the losses to his name not being on the ballot; The New York Times reported that others in his party dismissed that explanation and blamed him. The same night reset governor's offices from Texas outward, put a Canadian submarine purchase back in play, and put Hakeem Jeffries in line to lead the House.

### Lead
**Democrats Seize Control of Congress, Ending a G.O.P. Trifecta: The New York Times**
The New York Times reported that the Democratic Party wrested control of Congress from Republicans, and that Republicans lost both the House and the Senate, in what the paper called a wave of midterm victories and a stinging rebuke to President Trump's agenda. The Times reported that the House result ended a Republican trifecta and cemented divided government and a freshly assertive Congress after two years in which, the paper wrote, Republicans ceded power to President Trump. In a separate account, the Times reported that the backlash extended even into deep red states and, in the paper's reading, indicated that President Trump has lost his hold over the coalition that lifted him to the White House twice. The Times also reported a string of Senate victories in Iowa, Texas, and North and South Carolina, and wrote that Democrats flipped the Senate and the House with ease, leaving the president weakened. President Trump attributed the sweeping losses to the fact that he was not on the ballot. The Times reported that others in his party dismissed that explanation and pinned the blame squarely on him. He told the Times, "There was a mood in the air, I guess." On Truth Social, the BBC reported, he wrote that Republicans would have won "in a landslide" if his name had been on the ballot. The BBC's account was headlined that he takes aim at Republicans but says Democrats did a "good job." Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/04/us/politics/midterm-election-photos.html) Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/04/us/politics/democratic-midterms-wipeout.html) Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/04/us/elections/house-of-representatives-midterms-democrats-republicans.html) Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/04/us/politics/trump-republicans-blame-midterms.html) Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/04/us/politics/election-takeaways-democrats-win.html) Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/04/us/politics/midterm-election-rebuke-of-trump-era.html) Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/03/us/politics/senate-election-control.html) Source: [bbc.co.uk](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c6073l9y15xxo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss)

### Across the Region
**Gina Hinojosa Wins Texas Governor Race in Major Upset, Defeating Greg Abbott: The New York Times**
The New York Times reported that State Representative Gina Hinojosa defeated Governor Greg Abbott, denying him a fourth term, and that she is the first Hispanic candidate elected to lead Texas. The Times reported she concentrated on pocketbook issues, and that voters' opposition to Republican immigration policies was a tailwind. The same paper reported that victories by James Talarico and Gina Hinojosa upended decades of statewide Republican dominance in what had been the nation's most populous conservative state, a shift the Times described as once unthinkable. The paper called the night a Democratic rout that stunned Texas. Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/03/us/texas-governor-abbott-hinojosa.html) Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/04/us/gina-hinojosa-texas-governor.html) Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/04/us/texas-talarico-hinojosa-abbott-paxton.html)

**Canada looking to Germany for 8 submarines up front and 4 later: sources: CBC**
Canada is looking to split a planned purchase of twelve German submarines, committing to eight up front and leaving the remaining four for a future decision, sources told CBC News. CBC reported the proposal is intended to preserve financial flexibility. Those sources said the split could jeopardize some of the eighty-six billion dollars in economic benefits promised by Germany. The figures and the split come from sources speaking to CBC, not from a signed contract described in the report. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/canada-germany-submarines-defence-industry-economy-9.7407952?cmp=rss) Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/canada-germany-submarines-defence-industry-economy-9.7407952)

**Hakeem Jeffries is poised to become the first Black speaker of the House: NPR**
NPR reported that Hakeem Jeffries, a New York Democrat, is poised to become the first Black speaker of the House after House control was called for Democrats. As speaker he would be second in the presidential line of succession, after the vice president. He has vowed to focus on affordability and on holding the administration accountable. Addressing supporters, he argued that voters sent Congress a message to end extremism and "corruption." NPR headlined that he declares "America is back." The New York Times reported he would make history as the first Black speaker, and, in a separate account of what to know about him, that he was raised by a Black nationalist family in Brooklyn, is a moderate, and loves a hip-hop reference. The Times also reported that he told supporters, "We Hear You." Source: [npr.org](https://www.npr.org/2026/11/04/g-s1-150030/hakeem-jeffries-speaker-of-the-house-midterms) Source: [npr.org](https://www.npr.org/2026/11/04/nx-s1-6028572/hakeem-jeffries-midterms-house) Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/04/us/politics/hakeem-jeffries-what-to-know.html) Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/04/us/hakeem-jeffries-house.html)

### The Closer Look
**Public menopause care is scarce, and private care is costly. Why Canadians pay either way: The Globe and Mail**
Angela Rimmer has spent more than five thousand dollars out of pocket on menopause care that Ontario does not cover. She is forty-two, a single mother of four in the London, Ontario, area, and a full-time dental assistant. She told The Globe and Mail that brain fog, difficulty sleeping, night sweats, hot flashes, mood changes and exhaustion were debilitating, and that she needed treatment to keep working and to keep caregiving at home. A family doctor initially misdiagnosed her and wanted to prescribe antidepressants. She turned to two different private clinics for menopause hormone therapy. At one clinic she paid six hundred dollars for an initial assessment, two hundred dollars for each six-month follow-up, seventy dollars for lab tests, and about one hundred and twenty dollars a month in prescriptions. She has no private health insurance, and the province does not cover the treatments. She said, "I just wish that I didn't have to access this through private. I wish that it was in the public system, because we're having to pay so much." She said access, including the hormone therapy that has helped her, should be available without reaching so far into pocketbooks at the time when women should be saving for retirement and for their children's schooling. Private care, she said, has been costly and time-consuming to find.

The Globe and Mail reported that more than five million women in Canada are between forty and sixty, and that the majority will experience menopause symptoms, which can run from mild to overwhelming. Symptoms the paper listed range from fatigue to headaches, anxiety, muscle aches and heart palpitations. An Ipsos survey this year for GreenShield found that four in ten Canadian women do not know where to go for treatment, and that a third of respondents waited more than two years to get effective menopause care. The paper listed the barriers as a shortage of family physicians, doctors who lack training in menopause, long waits to see specialists, a dearth of research funding, and an explosion of misleading information online. Desperate for treatment, some women turn to private or virtual clinics. Some are run by physicians or nurse practitioners; others are operated by naturopaths or tech entrepreneurs. Women's health experts told the paper that the standard of care varies, and so do the prices, that many remedies are costly, and that not all are effective or safe. The paper reported that effective treatments exist that alleviate symptoms, and that most cases are not so complex that a family doctor cannot handle them. Currently, just two provinces, British Columbia and Manitoba, cover the costs of menopausal hormone therapy. Newer nonhormonal medications, Veozah and Lynkuet, which alleviate hot flashes and night sweats, are approved by Health Canada but are not fully covered by the public system. The Globe and Mail reported that Canada is behind Britain and Australia in taking steps to improve access. In June, the Society of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists of Canada warned that a two-tiered health system is emerging in which women are forced to pay for basic health care that should be free.

The Menopause Foundation of Canada says access should be universally available to all Canadians. It started a national campaign last month urging governments to bolster support for women experiencing menopause. The foundation says the widest gaps are for Indigenous, Black and racialized women, people living in rural communities, gender-diverse people and those with lower incomes. It said, "Access to safe, evidence-based menopause care should never depend on a person's ability to pay." Gynecologist and author Jen Gunter, of The Menopause Manifesto, said that whether someone lives in Flin Flon, Manitoba, or in downtown Toronto, they should be able to get excellent first-line menopause care, just as people should have access to care for blood pressure, and that these are things that should be available to everybody. In Lindsay, Ontario, Monika Kerschl-Sales, co-owner of Thairapy Beauty Bar, said she hears about menopause all the time, and that hundreds of women in the region who sit in her stylist chair have shared their struggles in getting care. She described her own perimenopause — low moods, fatigue, hot flashes, night sweats and brain fog — as a stretch when she did not feel like herself and could not bring her best to work. Source: [theglobeandmail.com](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/canada/article-menopause-health-care-public-private-clinics-costs/)

### Also Today
**Democrat Abdul El-Sayed defeats Republican Mike Rogers in key Michigan Senate race: NPR**
Abdul El-Sayed defeated Mike Rogers in Michigan's Senate race after a campaign NPR described as testing an antiestablishment candidate on the left in a perennial Midwest battleground, and with the win he will be the first Muslim American to serve in the Senate. Source: [npr.org](https://www.npr.org/2026/11/04/g-s1-150029/michigan-senate-race-abdul-el-sayed-mike-rogers)

**Troy Jackson wins Maine Senate race over Susan Collins, in major coup for Democrats: NPR**
Troy Jackson defeated Susan Collins in Maine, NPR reported, flipping a Senate seat she had held for nearly thirty years and ending three decades in the Senate for the sole Republican representing New England in Congress, as The New York Times put it. Source: [npr.org](https://www.npr.org/2026/11/04/g-s1-148952/maine-senate-race-susan-collins-troy-jackson) Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/04/us/elections/maine-senate-collins-jackson.html)

**Democrat Christina Bohannan wins election to U.S. House in Iowa's 1st Congressional District: PBS**
PBS reported that Democrat Christina Bohannan won election to the U.S. House in Iowa's 1st Congressional District, and The New York Times reported she unseated Representative Mariannette Miller-Meeks, with discontent about the war with Iran and tariffs helping create a tough environment for the defeated Republican. Source: [pbs.org](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/democrat-christina-bohannan-wins-election-to-u-s-house-in-iowas-1st-congressional-district) Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/04/us/politics/iowa-house-1-bohannan-miller-meeks.html)

**As a New Brunswick pulp mill goes quiet, a forestry town waits for the axe to fall: The Globe and Mail**
In Nackawic, New Brunswick, the pulp mill across the river emitted what might have been its last puff of smoke last week, and the town's largest employer for half a century is shutting down because of "prevailing market conditions," according to the India-based owner, AV Group New Brunswick. Source: [theglobeandmail.com](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/canada/article-as-a-new-brunswick-pulp-mill-goes-quiet-a-forestry-town-waits-for-the/)

**No catastrophic financial hit required to fight climate change, scientists say in landmark court case: CBC**
In a Vancouver courtroom this week, one of Canada's leading climate scientists testified during a landmark trial that Canada does not need to shut down its industries or take a catastrophic financial hit to effectively fight climate change, CBC reported. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/science/climate-lawsuit-canada-vancouver-testimony-9.7408076?cmp=rss)

**Russia Will Not Compete at World Junior Hockey Championship in Canada, PM Carney Says: The Moscow Times**
Russia will not compete at the World Junior Hockey Championship in Canada, Prime Minister Mark Carney said, The Moscow Times reported. Source: [themoscowtimes.com](https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2026/11/04/russia-will-not-compete-at-world-junior-hockey-championship-in-canada-pm-carney-says-a94174)

### Progress Watch
**Haaland and Flanagan, Two Native American Women, Break Political Barriers: The New York Times**
The New York Times reported that Deb Haaland of New Mexico will be the nation's first woman Native American governor, and that Peggy Flanagan, Minnesota's next senator, is the first Native American woman to win election to that chamber. The Times reported Flanagan, the state's lieutenant governor, defeated former sports broadcaster Michele Tafoya and keeps the Minnesota Senate seat in Democratic hands. Those results put a Native American woman in a governorship and another in the Senate for the first time the paper records. Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/04/us/elections/haaland-flanagan-native-american-women-elected.html) Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/04/us/minnesota-senate-tafoya-flanagan.html)

episodes.episode_title: Ep 38: Democrats gained two hundred fifty-eight statehouse seats, resetting who writes law in…
episodes.content:
# Omni View North America
> **Democrats gained two hundred fifty-eight statehouse seats, resetting who writes law in state capitals.**

**What You Need to Know:** Democrats gained 258 state legislative seats in Tuesday’s midterms, according to State Navigate, resetting who holds chambers and governorships across the United States. Two Senate races were still uncalled, including Mississippi, where Scott Colom led Cindy Hyde-Smith by 1,138 votes and the state has no recount law. In Canada, Mark Carney tables a second budget on Thursday that a Fraser Institute commentator says deepens deficits younger taxpayers will carry.

### Lead
**Democrats Gain Hundreds of State Legislative Seats: The Guardian**
Democrats gained 258 state legislative seats in Tuesday’s midterm elections, according to Chaz Nuttycombe, executive director of State Navigate, creating six new governing trifectas, taking 11 legislative chambers from Republicans and breaking Republican supermajorities in 10 states. The Guardian reports that ballots are still being counted, and that the party has not held full control of government in Arizona in 60 years, in Pennsylvania since the 1990s, or in Wisconsin since 2010, while Michigan and Minnesota regained trifectas lost after the 2024 election. In Texas, Democrats will control the state house for the first time since 2002. The New York Times reports they won control of state governments in Wisconsin, Michigan, Minnesota, Pennsylvania and Nevada, and won chambers in Texas, Georgia and North Carolina. They also won gubernatorial races over Republicans in Georgia, Iowa, Nevada, Ohio and Texas, a majority of governorships for the first time since 2010, the Guardian reports. Mandara Meyers, executive director of the States Project, said it was the most significant night for state legislative power since the Republican wave of 2010, and that Democrats now have more power in the states than at any other point in the 21st century. Nuttycombe predicts about 76 percent of the population will live under a Democratic governor and about half will be represented by a Democratic lawmaker in their legislature, and he said roughly 80 to 85 percent of the wave is the economy and dissatisfaction with the president. The Guardian says Democrats are on course for a Senate majority of at least 54 seats and 237 House seats. Andy Beshear of Kentucky and Gretchen Whitmer of Michigan, leaders of the Democratic Governors Association, said more Democratic governors mean better lives for the millions of Americans who live in their states. Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/05/democrats-state-legislatures-midterm-elections) Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/04/us/politics/state-legislatures-democrats-midterm-election.html)

### Across the Region
**Mississippi Senate Race Leads by 1,138 Votes, and the State Has No Recount Law: The Guardian**
Almost 24 hours after Democrats secured control of Congress, two Senate seats were still in play, with counting in Alaska expected to continue into Thursday. In Mississippi, Democrat Scott Colom led Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith by 1,138 votes with almost 96 percent counted, the Guardian reports, and new batches had not been reported for several hours even as Colom’s votes had been outpacing hers. Mississippi has no law for initiating a recount; The New York Times reports the state does not allow vote recounts in statewide elections. Democrats have not won a U.S. Senate seat in Mississippi since 1982, Donald Trump carried the state by 22 points in 2024, and the state has not elected a Black person to that office since 1875. Colom, a seventh-generation Mississippian whose father was a Republican, became the first Black district attorney for the 16th circuit in 2015 and, as district attorney, had a 94 percent success rate for convictions. Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/live/2026/nov/05/midterm-elections-live-latest-updates-mississippi-senate-race) Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/04/us/mississippi-senate-election-recount-law.html)

**Triumphal Arch Set to Win Final Approval Despite Court Challenges: The New York Times**
After court challenges to the project, a federal planning board is expected to give final approval on Thursday to President Trump’s 250-foot triumphal arch, The New York Times reports. NPR reports the panel meets Thursday and the government said it may begin construction later that same day. Critics hope a judge will intervene at the last minute. The Times reports court action and Democrats’ upcoming control of Congress could halt the plans. Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/05/us/politics/trump-triumphal-arch-planning-commission.html) Source: [npr.org](https://www.npr.org/2026/11/05/nx-s1-6027301/trump-arch-federal-approval-judge-construction)

### The Closer Look
**What to watch for as Carney introduces his 2nd federal budget: CBC**
Prime Minister Mark Carney’s government tables its second federal budget on Thursday, since taking office in March 2025. The CBC says the budget is the next step in a plan to support the country through an affordability crunch and the trade war. A Globe and Mail headline in the same day’s coverage says Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne has said the budget will focus on affordability and cultural sovereignty.

Jake Fuss, director of fiscal studies at the Fraser Institute, argues in The Globe and Mail that Canadians should expect more new spending and large deficits. He writes that Carney promised on the campaign trail a “very different approach” to federal finances from Justin Trudeau, and later said he would be “spending less,” then increased spending significantly. Fuss says the government posted a $66.9-billion deficit for 2025-26, a projected deficit of $65.3-billion in 2026-27, and deficits of at least $53-billion for each of the subsequent four years. Those cumulative deficits from 2025-26 to 2029-30, he writes, are double what Trudeau planned before leaving office. Ottawa has not balanced a budget in nearly 20 years, he notes, after the Trudeau government borrowed hundreds of billions and pushed inflation-adjusted per-person spending and debt to historically high levels.

To cover the deficit, Ottawa must borrow. Fuss says total federal debt will eclipse a projected $2.9-trillion by 2029-30 — almost $300-billion more than Trudeau planned — and that debt interest costs will hit a projected $75.7-billion, more than the combined total Ottawa plans to spend that year on employment insurance and the Canada Child Benefit. He argues the burden lands disproportionately on younger Canadians, who are likely to pay higher taxes, enjoy fewer services, or both. He also argues that when the government borrows, it competes with individuals, families and businesses, and that lenders raise interest rates, making mortgages, cars and renovations more expensive. He says today’s higher interest rates exist in part because of federal and provincial spending and borrowing.

Last year, Fuss writes, the Carney government separated “operating spending” — day-to-day programs such as Old Age Security and employment insurance — from “capital spending,” defined as “anything that builds an asset,” and said last month it would balance the operating budget by 2028-29. He says both categories affect the bottom line, and that the split obscures the true state of federal finances. The Parliamentary Budget Officer has criticized how the government classifies capital spending, he writes, because the government has an incentive to shift items from operating to capital. A separate PBO report last month said the government is not on track to balance the operating budget by 2028-29 regardless of that classification. Fuss’s conclusion is that, absent substantial spending reductions or huge jumps in revenue, the overall deficit remains larger than the Trudeau government’s projections, and that younger Canadians inherit the bill. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/carney-second-federal-budget-lookahead-9.7409464?cmp=rss) Source: [theglobeandmail.com](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/business/commentary/article-carney-federal-budget-younger-canadians-will-pay-for-massive-spending/)

### Also Today
**Some Americans Turn to Libraries as Prices Stay High: NPR**
NPR reports some Americans squeezed by high prices are relying more on local libraries for books, streaming services and high-priced items such as musical instruments and sewing machines. Source: [npr.org](https://www.npr.org/2026/11/05/nx-s1-5992908/libraries-and-cost-of-living)

**A Democratic Congress Would Struggle to Move Fuel Prices Directly: NPR**
NPR reports a new Democratic majority could pressure the president to end the war in Iran, but fuel prices are tied to a complex international oil market and will be harder for Congress to affect directly. Source: [npr.org](https://www.npr.org/2026/11/05/nx-s1-6029365/gas-diesel-price-congress-midterms)

**Justice Alito Tells Friends He Will Not Retire Before the Term Ends: The New York Times**
