episodes.content:
# Omni View North America
> **Governor Newsom commuted all five hundred forty-eight California death sentences, a quarter of the national total.**

**What You Need to Know:** Governor Newsom commuted all five hundred forty-eight California death sentences, a quarter of the national total. He called capital punishment morally objectionable, and California has not carried out an execution in twenty years. The Times reports he is considering a presidential run; Austin Sarat writes in The Guardian that emptying death row frees hundreds from the threat of execution.

### Lead
**Newsom Commutes the Sentences of California’s 548 Death Row Inmates: The New York Times**
Governor Gavin Newsom commuted the sentences of California’s 548 people on death row, The New York Times reports. He called capital punishment morally objectionable. The Times reports he is considering a run for president, and that California has not executed anyone for 20 years. Those 548 sentences are about a quarter of death sentences nationwide, the Times reports. In The Guardian, Austin Sarat writes that the decision to empty the state’s death row frees hundreds of people from the threat of execution. Sarat, treating Newsom as a politician who may seek the presidency, argues that the move signals opposition to the death penalty is no longer a third rail in US politics. Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/05/us/california-death-row-newsom-commutation.html) Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2026/nov/06/california-gavin-newsom-death-row-history)

### Across the Region
**Carney's bet on economic growth — and the risks that come with it: CBC**
Prime Minister Mark Carney’s budget bets that Ottawa can borrow billions now for major projects meant to jump-start the economy, CBC reports, and CBC says a failed payoff would leave Canada’s debt load exposed to new risks. Bloomberg reports the budget spends an oil windfall on housing and investment measures. On defence, CBC reports a path to 157 billion dollars in annual spending by 2030, closer to NATO’s five per cent target, with few details on rearmament and no roadmap past 2030. The Globe and Mail reports Ottawa is easing off defence increases, with no further progress toward the military spending target beyond 2027-28, while CBC says analysts question whether fiscal pressure and shifting priorities will undermine the commitments. Leaders of the Bloc Québécois, the NDP and the Green Party told The Globe and Mail the budget was disappointing, lacked substance and did not do enough on affordability. The Globe and Mail also reports a 4 billion dollar cultural-sector boost for national museums, art galleries, journalism and a new national digital library, framed as support for national sovereignty. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/business/armstrong-canada-budget-2026-economy-risks-9.7411557?cmp=rss) Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/defence-budget-military-nato-trump-9.7411329?cmp=rss) Source: [bloomberg.com](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/newsletters/2026-11-05/canada-budget-2026-carney-spends-oil-windfall-on-tax-measures-housing-plan) Source: [theglobeandmail.com](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/politics/article-federal-budget-defence-spending-2026-canada/) Source: [theglobeandmail.com](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/canada/video-opposition-leaders-react-to-2026-budget/) Source: [theglobeandmail.com](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/politics/article-federal-budget-2026-canada-culture-national-identity-sovereignty/)

**A judge blocks construction of Trump's arch moments after it won federal approval: NPR**
A day after the triumphal arch sat on the verge of approval, a federal judge blocked construction for 14 days, NPR reports, moments after a federal panel approved it late Thursday. District Judge Tanya Chutkan ordered the hold while the court weighs legality; NPR reports the administration had hoped to start at once, and the order came just after midnight. Euronews reports the National Capital Planning Commission approved a 250-foot arch, inspired by Paris’s Arc de Triomphe, beside Arlington National Cemetery. Representative Jared Huffman, a California Democrat, told the commission the arch would dishonour America and disrupt the link between the Lincoln Memorial and the cemetery, and he called it a tribute to Donald Trump. Greg Wischer of the Interior Department said it would fulfil a 100-year plan for a monumental work on Columbia Island. President Trump has said the structure would become a top-grade military complex to house drones, snipers and ammunition, Euronews reports. Source: [npr.org](https://www.npr.org/2026/11/06/nx-s1-6031990/trump-arch-planning-commission-injunction) Source: [euronews.com](https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/06/judge-blocks-construction-of-trumps-massive-triumphal-arch)

**1 Officer Is Killed and 3 Are Wounded in Shootout on Suburban Denver Bus: The New York Times**
One police officer was killed and three were wounded after a man opened fire on officers who pursued him onto a bus in Lakewood, Colorado, The New York Times reports, citing the authorities. A civilian was also injured. The authorities said police shot the gunman dead. Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/06/us/lakewood-police-shooting-colorado-bus-dead.html)

### The Closer Look
**Online gambling more than doubles among young Montreal men, study finds: Global News**
Online gambling has more than doubled among men aged 18 to 34 in Montreal, even as the share of adults who gamble at all has fallen, Global News reports from a new public health study. Researchers surveyed 8,500 Montreal adults. Thirty-nine per cent said they had gambled in some form in 2025, 15 per cent fewer than in 2018 and in 2002. The authors say the line runs the other way for younger men: the number who reported gambling online has more than doubled.

Sylvia Kairouz, a Concordia University gambling researcher and one of the authors, said the phone is the mechanism. When a person only has to pick up a phone and push a button, she said, resisting is very difficult. She said researchers have seen more interest in online gambling than in casinos or any other physical location.

Anne Elizabeth Lapointe, chief executive of Maison Jean Lapointe, which offers treatment for gambling addiction, said the study matches the people coming through the door. She told Global News on Thursday that more and more young men are seeking help for online gambling addiction. Since the COVID pandemic, she said, the organization has been helping far fewer people struggling with in-person slots or video lottery terminals, while online gambling has become the growing concern. She said even minors are finding ways to gamble online. For the last two years, she said, kids have come to the office with a gambling addiction or with serious consequences from the habit, and young people with little or no income can face serious consequences from their losses.

The earlier steps the sources name are that pandemic-era shift away from physical machines, and the spread of advertising. Kairouz said the volume of gambling advertising is making sports betting more socially acceptable. The study found 75 per cent of those surveyed wished there were no advertisements at all for gambling sites. Lapointe said gambling advertising needs to be banned or regulated more effectively.

The figures land on men 18 to 34, on minors who reach the sites, and on the clinics treating them. For anyone who still bets, Kairouz recommends setting a budget and sticking to it. She said that over the long term, people who bet on sports will lose money because unpredictable outcomes are unavoidable, and that the house always wins. Help is available across Canada for gambling-related problems. In Quebec, Gambling: Help and Referral offers free, confidential support around the clock, in Montreal and elsewhere in the province, including online. Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12139130/online-gambling-betting-doubles-montreal-men/)

### Also Today

The Guardian reports Democrats lead Republicans 253 to 157 in the House with 25 races still uncalled, and that Nithya Raman, a democratic socialist, won the Los Angeles mayor’s race over incumbent Karen Bass, while Republican Senator Ted Cruz called the election a Watergate-level repudiation. Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/live/2026/nov/06/us-midterm-elections-2026-democrats-blue-wave-congress-latest-news-updates)

United Airlines will cancel all its remaining flights to Tulum starting in January, Mexico News Daily reports, while Air Canada, WestJet, Air Transat, Viva and Mexicana keep their Tulum routes. Source: [mexiconewsdaily.com](https://mexiconewsdaily.com/travel/united-airlines-cancels-all-remaining-flights-tulum-starting-january/)

**Low birth rates were emptying public schools. ICE deportations are now making it worse: NPR**
NPR reports school enrollment was already expected to fall by 2 million children by 2030, and education experts say deportations of immigrant families with school-age children are deepening that drop. Source: [npr.org](https://www.npr.org/2026/11/06/nx-s1-5971283/public-school-enrollment-ice-deportation-birthrate)

**Voters in 4 States Limit Trans Athletes: The New York Times**
Voters in Arizona, Colorado, Nebraska and Washington approved bans on transgender athletes on female sports teams, The New York Times reports, and organizers of the measures said the results were likely to lead to similar ballot efforts elsewhere. Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/05/us/transgender-athlete-bans-referendums.html)

**Elections Alberta says referendum cost $84-million, exceeding agency’s annual budget: The Globe and Mail**
Elections Alberta says a separatism referendum cost 84 million dollars, nearly 50 million dollars beyond what its annual budget can pay, and that it needs the province to cover the rest, The Globe and Mail reports. Source: [theglobeandmail.com](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/canada/alberta/article-elections-alberta-separation-referendum-cost-84-million/) Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12139021/elections-alberta-referendum-cost/)

**Tenants upset with squalid conditions at central Edmonton apartment building: Global News**
Tenants at an apartment building in Edmonton’s McCauley neighbourhood have gone a week without working water and heat, Global News reports, in a building that shows disrepair outside and evidence of drug use inside. Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12139111/edmonton-mccauley-apartment-building-living-conditions/)

**Ottawa reviewing circumstances of Indigenous woman’s death after she missed postsurgery appointments: The Globe and Mail**
Ottawa is reviewing the death of Miranda Mamakwa, an Indigenous woman who missed postsurgery appointments, after her family asked the Ontario Provincial Police commissioner to investigate federal officials for criminal negligence, The Globe and Mail reports. Source: [theglobeandmail.com](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/canada/article-ottawa-reviewing-indigenous-womans-death-missed-postsurgery/)

**Hockey’s streaming spree means there’s one fewer thing holding Canada together: The Guardian**
The Guardian reports nine Edmonton Oilers games this season, and a handful of games for each Canadian NHL team, are available only with a 12.99 dollar monthly Sportsnet+ subscription from Rogers, with some other games only on Amazon Prime. Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/nov/06/hockeys-streaming-spree-means-theres-one-fewer-thing-holding-canada-together)

### Both Sides: Whether a president can lock the Oval Office as a national monument
President Donald Trump has signed an executive order declaring the Oval Office a national monument, and the fight is over whether that order can stop a successor from altering it. Trump’s case, as he put it to reporters, is that the room is a symbol of the country and should not be touched, destroyed or ripped down by a later president in order to build something in a slightly different shape. He said the White House and the Oval Office had been badly damaged before his changes, describing broken windows, cracked walls and broken stone, and he said the order would make it impossible for anybody to destroy the space.

The order’s own text, as the BBC reports it, cuts the other way: it does not restrict a president’s authority to redecorate, select furnishings, or make ordinary operational and security changes that do not substantially impair the historic structure. Greg Werkheiser, of the law firm Cultural Heritage Partners, told the BBC that furniture and decor are already up to the president so long as permanent art and architecture are not damaged, and he called the order legally meaningless because Trump cannot bind a successor this way. Werkheiser called it hypocrisy beside the demolition of the East Wing, a project the BBC reports was not approved by Congress and is continuing as a ballroom, and beside what he described as lawsuits aimed at weakening preservation law. The grounds are already a National Historic Landmark. Trump himself scaled back two national monuments in Utah in 2017, and the BBC reports that revoking a monument designation has not been tested in court, so it is unclear whether a future president or a lawsuit could undo this order. Source: [bbc.co.uk](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cmy0eeg101djo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss)

episodes.content:
# Omni View North America
> **Stephen Miller replaces Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff, sharpening Trump's immigration line.**

**What You Need to Know:** Stephen Miller is the new White House chief of staff after President Donald Trump, on Friday afternoon, said on Truth Social that Miller would replace Susie Wiles and confirmed she had been ousted. The Guardian describes Miller as Trump's most trusted adviser and as the architect of his sweeping immigration crackdown, and it reports the change in the wake of the midterm elections. The Guardian says Democrats and Republicans criticized the promotion, and that Democratic lawmakers called Miller a hatemonger, a xenophobe and vile.

### Lead
**Trump faces criticism for ‘dangerous’ Stephen Miller appointment as White House chief of staff: The Guardian US**
On Friday afternoon, President Donald Trump abruptly announced on his Truth Social platform that Stephen Miller would replace Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff, and he confirmed that Wiles had been ousted. The Guardian describes Miller as Trump's most trusted adviser. It also describes him as the architect of Trump's sweeping immigration crackdown, the record the appointment puts at the center of the West Wing. The Guardian places the announcement in the wake of the U.S. midterm elections. It reports that Democrats and Republicans criticized the promotion. Democratic lawmakers, the Guardian reports, decried Miller as a hatemonger, a xenophobe and vile. The criticism, as the Guardian presents it, is aimed at the person now running the White House staff operation, not at a proposal still awaiting a decision. For the immigration apparatus Miller has led, the change puts that adviser in the chief of staff's chair after the midterms rather than leaving Wiles in the post. Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/07/stephen-miller-democrats-react)

### Across the Region
**Canada's military is using Palantir software. What are the risks?: CBC Politics**
Canada has multimillion-dollar contracts with the U.S. technology firm Palantir, and the Canadian military is using the company's software. Experts warn that the deals could expose military data to U.S. authorities. They also warn that the contracts could deepen Canada's reliance on foreign technology. The Department of National Defence says its systems keep government data secure in Canada. The dispute, as CBC reports it, is over where that data can be reached and how dependent the military becomes, not over whether the contracts exist. For Canadian defence systems that now run on Palantir software, the experts' warning and the department's assurance are the two accounts on the table. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/palantir-canadian-military-9.7409099?cmp=rss)

**Mysterious Request Scrambles Major Supreme Court Gun Case Against Cook County: The New York Times US**
The lead plaintiff in one of two cases challenging semiautomatic weapons bans has asked to drop out, the New York Times reports. The request comes weeks before the cases are heard. The Times calls the move unusual. It says the request scrambles a major Supreme Court case against Cook County. The case is one of two on those bans, so the withdrawal request hits the lead plaintiff in a paired set of challenges rather than a lone filing. For Cook County's semiautomatic weapons ban, the Times reports that the challenge reaching the Court has been scrambled before argument by the plaintiff's own request to leave the case. Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/07/us/politics/supreme-court-guns-plaintiff.html)

**Houston Police to Stop Alerting ICE During Traffic Stops: The New York Times US**
Mayor John Whitmire has instructed Houston police to stop notifying immigration agents when they encounter someone without legal status during routine street stops, the New York Times reports. The instruction applies to those routine street stops, not to a broader rewrite of federal immigration law. Houston officers, under the mayor's order, are no longer to alert Immigration and Customs Enforcement in that encounter. For people without legal status stopped on Houston streets, the change is in whether local police make that notification. The Times attributes the instruction to Whitmire. Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/06/us/houston-mayor-john-whitmire-immigration-ice-cooperation.html)

### The Closer Look
**One of Okanagan’s most colourful characters dies at 96: Global News Canada**
Eddy Haymour died on Wednesday at the age of 96. For decades, a distinctive castle overlooking Highway 97 in Peachland has served as a reminder of him. Global News reports that he leaves a story of ambition, controversy and a dream that never quite came to fruition. For many locals, his name is synonymous with both the castle and Rattlesnake Island. Okanagan resident Don Scramstad put it this way: “Rattlesnake island and a bit of trouble, a lot of trouble.”

Haymour, a Lebanese immigrant, purchased Rattlesnake Island in 1971 with plans to transform the five-acre property into a Middle Eastern-themed amusement park. That vision caught the attention of filmmaker Greg Crompton, who produced the 2019 documentary “Eddy’s Kingdom.” Crompton told Global News that, when ideas were being kicked around, this one seemed a compelling story to tell. “So I was quite motivated personally but also as a filmmaker, I want to tell interesting stories. This is a very interesting story,” Crompton said.

The dispute with the provincial government escalated in 1974, when Haymour and his relatives took hostages at the Canadian embassy in Beirut. Crompton said Haymour’s rationale was the most interesting part of him, and described a thought process in Haymour’s own framing: wronged by the government, then “you were going to get some grenades and chuck it into the legislature and and cause mayhem.” Crompton said that thought process was maybe the most compelling part. At the Peachland Museum, Haymour remains a prominent figure in the community’s history. Assistant curator Jeff Green said, “He was zealously committed to his dream,” and that it did not matter what obstacle was in his way; he pursued it to the end.

Haymour eventually won his legal battle with the province. His dream of developing the island never materialized. He did build the castle in Peachland, and beside it a statue of himself pointing across the lake toward the island he had big dreams for. Tracy Janes, a customer service agent at the museum, said, “He was a visionary. He was impassioned about what he was doing,” and that everything about the man was larger than life. For Peachland, the castle on Highway 97 and the statue aimed at Rattlesnake Island are what remain of a five-acre plan from 1971, a 1974 hostage-taking in Beirut, a legal win against the province, and a development that never rose on the island. Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12140696/okanagans-colourful-character-dies-96-eddy-haymour/)

### Also Today
**Northern, remote RCMP detachments chronically and critically understaffed: internal report: CBC Politics**

Foreign Affairs Minister Anita Anand is pressing G7 allies to intensify pressure on Russia after an attack on a Ukrainian aid distribution site killed 53 people. For Canada’s place in those rooms, Anand is tying a civilian death toll she cites to sanctions, military support, and a direct confrontation with Moscow in December. episodes.episode_title: Ep 41: Abbott sent thousands of Guardsmen to the Texas border, and then he lost.
episodes.content:
# Omni View North America

> **Abbott sent thousands of Guardsmen to the Texas border, and then he lost.**

**What You Need to Know:** Abbott sent thousands of Guardsmen to the Texas border, and then he lost. The San Antonio Express-News asks what comes next for that deployment, while governor-elect Gina Hinojosa, in her first New York Times interview since the victory, talked about data centers, abortion restrictions and Elon Musk. The Times also describes a Democratic plan to reverse hard-line immigration policies and fresh momentum to curb aggressive ICE tactics.

### Lead
**Abbott sent thousands of Guardsmen to the border. He lost. Now what?: San Antonio Express-News**
The San Antonio Express-News reports that Greg Abbott sent thousands of Guardsmen to the border and that he lost, and it asks what comes next. Gina Hinojosa, whom The New York Times identifies as governor-elect, used her first interview with the paper since that victory to talk about tackling data centers, abortion restrictions and Elon Musk. In a companion report, the Times says Texas led on hard-line immigration policies and that Democrats plan a reversal. The paper says a Democratic sweep in the state signals fresh momentum to curb aggressive ICE tactics across a shifting national landscape on immigration. For the Guardsmen Abbott sent, the Express-News leaves the deployment's future as the open question after his loss. For Texans, Hinojosa's interview puts data centers, abortion restrictions and Elon Musk on the incoming governor's stated agenda, while the Times describes the immigration change as a Democratic plan and the sweep as a signal, not as a completed statute. Source: [expressnews.com](https://www.expressnews.com/news/article/hinojosa-texas-guard-border-mission-in-jeopardy-22512786.php) Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/08/us/gina-hinojosa-texas-priorities.html) Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/08/us/texas-border-immigration-ice.html)

### Across the Region
**Poilievre pans Liberal budget's $15M capital gains exemption, calls for 'simpler' plan: CBC**

He argues that a proposed $15-million capital gains exemption on the sale of qualifying shares from a Canadian company applies too narrowly and excludes key businesses. He is calling for a simpler plan. The measure, as CBC describes it, is a proposal inside the latest budget, and the fight is over which sellers of Canadian-company shares would qualify. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/poilievre-capital-gains-exemption-budget-2026-9.7413640?cmp=rss) Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/poilievre-capital-gains-exemption-budget-2026-9.7413640)

**UFC's Dana White says he will meet with Trump Monday over offer to be White House press secretary: NPR**
President Donald Trump said Saturday that he has offered the job of White House press secretary to his friend and UFC boss Dana White, NPR reports. The New York Times reports that the offer came on social media, that the job is now vacant, that White is the organization's CEO, and that the president told him to bring along fighters as aides. NPR reports that White says he will meet with Trump on Monday over the offer. The dated next step in that account is Monday's meeting, over a post the Times describes as vacant and over aides the president said should include fighters. Source: [npr.org](https://www.npr.org/2026/11/08/nx-s1-6033900/ufc-dana-white-trump-white-house-press-secretary) Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/07/us/politics/trump-dana-white-ufc-press-secretary.html)

**Judge Taps Lawyer to Investigate Trump Administration’s Conduct in Golf Course Case: The New York Times**
Judge Ana C. Reyes wrote that she intended to pick a former U.S. attorney in Washington to investigate whether officials misled the court about changes to the East Potomac Golf Links, The New York Times reports. The move is an intended appointment to investigate, and the question the judge set is whether officials misled the court. What changes for the Trump administration's handling of those golf-course changes is a court inquiry into that conduct, not a finding already made. Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/07/us/politics/washington-judge-special-master-trump-golf.html)

### The Closer Look
**Daughter of WWII veteran selling ‘door poppies’ to support local Legion: Global News Canada**
As Remembrance Day approaches, Margot Rockett is working hard to keep up with demand after her craftsmanship went viral on TikTok, Global News reports. She makes what she calls door poppies: large, wreath-like poppies that can be hung on doors, walls and windows. She told Global News it is a bigger, bolder way to say she remembers. Each door poppy costs $10 and is officially licensed by the Legion. She said the policy is rigid and strict because the poppy is a trademarked image, and she said she respects that because the Legion has to protect it. All of the proceeds go to her Legion branch at Coxwell and Gerrard. She said all of the money stays in the community to support local veterans and their families.

The craft has a family history the article dates in stages. Rockett's father served in the Air Force in the Second World War. In the last few years of his life, she said, he lived at the Sunnybrook Veterans Centre. She said they took such good care of him that she wanted to give back to the Poppy Fund and to the Legion. During the pandemic, she said, the door poppy was born: she tweaked a flower she had made before and made the door poppy.

The branch treats the money as operating support for its own poppy campaign. Shelley Lyons, vice-president at the Coxwell and Gerrard Legion, told Global News that when Rockett approached them a couple of years ago, Lyons thought it was pretty amazing, and that proceeds coming to this branch specifically for the poppy campaign are a huge income for the branch. Lyons said it has been disheartening to see fewer people wearing poppies around Remembrance Day, and she hopes Rockett's initiative will encourage people to pay their respects. She said that as the First and Second World Wars fade further into history, a lack of education and memory knowledge could be driving factors. She said it always makes her smile when she sees someone wearing a poppy. Rockett is working all hours to keep up with demand and said she would not have it any other way. She said that if her dad were here, he would be really proud. Global News credited Sean O'Shea among the files on the story. Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12141371/door-poppy-remembrance-day/)

episodes.content:
# Omni View North America
> **Trump now offers a ten-year stay deal so some long-term immigrants can remain.**

**What You Need to Know:** President Trump is offering a ten-year stay deal so some long-term undocumented immigrants can remain, after telling CBS's 60 Minutes that his deportation policy was too tough. He said people convicted of serious crimes should still be removed, days after Stephen Miller was elevated to White House chief of staff. He also linked much of the Republican midterm defeat to the war with Iran and higher petrol prices.

### Lead
**Trump admits deportation policy was 'too tough' despite promotion of Stephen Miller: The Guardian**
On CBS's 60 Minutes on Sunday, President Trump told correspondent Ross Douthat that he thought his deportation policy was "too tough," and that he was open to an arrangement letting some undocumented immigrants remain. Asked whether the policy had gone too far, he said, "I think it might be too tough, yeah," adding that a lot of people would say it is great and a lot of people think it is too tough. He said people here for 10 or 15 years should "work a deal," while removal continued for killers, rapists and drug dealers, and he called that "something that's actually doable." He said the policy "both helped and hurt": an "A+" for closing the border and "very high marks for getting the bad ones out," but political damage because people with good jobs were removed for the violation of entering illegally. The Guardian reports those comments sit against Friday's elevation of Stephen Miller, whom it calls the architect of the crackdown, to White House chief of staff. The same account says that since Trump returned to office, Immigration and Customs Enforcement raids at workplaces, homes and public spaces have ensnared people with no criminal records, separated families and spread fear in immigrant communities, and that federal agents fatally shot two US citizens, Renee Good and Alex Pretti, during operations in Minneapolis this year. Trump said some people believe undocumented immigrants should stay if they are "good people working in a landscaping company" and in some cases paying taxes; he said some Democrats had already contacted him, and that he could refrain from name-calling for six months "very easily." He agreed with Vice President JD Vance that the war with Iran was a significant factor in the Republican midterm defeat, also citing higher petrol prices and what he called a growing dislike of Israel, while saying he would make the same decision again because "you can't let Iran have a nuclear weapon," that the war had been won, and that a renewed assault was something he was not looking to escalate after the midterms. In a separate CNN interview he called a renewed assault "highly unlikely," depending on "whether or not they sign a very strong agreement"; on the economy he said the administration had failed to communicate despite his claims of record employment, investment and stock-market figures, and "it was bad messaging, maybe by me"; on artificial intelligence, "I don't mind guardrails," but not a "deep second position." Douthat cited a Forbes estimate that Trump's net worth rose by $3 billion from the autumn of 2024 to the autumn of 2025. Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/09/trump-tells-60-minutes-deportation-policy-too-tough-ice-immigration) · [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/08/us/politics/trump-immigration-crackdown-republicans-midterms.html)

### Across the Region
**After losing Congress, Republicans have one last shot to pass their agenda: The Washington Post**
Republicans, having lost Congress, have what The Washington Post calls one last shot to pass their agenda. The New York Times reports that an impeachment vote on the defense secretary, a spending deal and several major bills are in play in a post-election session shaped by last week's election. NPR reports lawmakers return to Washington this week, and that Republicans plan to finish work on several outstanding issues before Democrats take control of Congress in January. The Times also reports that, following their midterm victories, Democrats are preparing to open wide-ranging investigations into President Trump, his family and his administration, and that congressional reporter Michael Gold identifies the Democrats' biggest targets. The Washington Post frames the returning session as the remaining window for the Republican agenda after the loss of Congress; the Times describes the agenda of that session as hazy. Source: [washingtonpost.com](https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/2026/11/09/republicans-have-one-last-shot-pass-their-agenda-after-losing-congress/) · [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/09/us/politics/congress-republicans-agenda-lame-duck-session.html) · [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/video/us/politics/100000011266496/democrats-plan-corruption-investigations-after-election-victory.html) · [npr.org](https://www.npr.org/2026/11/09/nx-s1-6030633/congress-is-coming-back-to-washington-heres-what-to-expect)

**Ottawa poised to seal trade deal with Philippines, now home to Canada's second-biggest embassy: The Globe and Mail**
Carney arrives Saturday on a trip that also includes a European leaders' meeting in Ireland, the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in China, and the Francophonie summit in Cambodia. Global Affairs spokesperson Aditee Kissoon said the Manila mission had about 300 positions as of early October, counting locally hired staff and officials from federal departments, provincial governments and Crown corporations, second only to Washington by headcount, with London, Mexico City and Delhi next. Under the 2022 Indo-Pacific strategy, Canada has shared Dark Vessel Detection satellite data to help Manila track illegal fishing and Chinese coast guard ships, including CCG-5901, which a Philippine Coast Guard spokesman publicly acknowledged in 2024 and which Manila has accused of intimidation; the Globe says the program's primary purpose is fighting overfishing, including vessels Manila believes are part of Beijing's maritime militia, and that the data has also helped track coast guard ships enforcing disputed claims in the South China Sea, where the Philippines has clashed with Beijing over reefs and shoals and where its northernmost islands sit near a gateway to the open Pacific, a short distance from Taiwan, which the Globe describes as a self-governed island of about 23 million people claimed by China. The embassy now hosts the Indo-Pacific Agriculture and Agri-Food Office, opened in 2024, and an Export Development Canada office opened the same year; Citizenship and Immigration operations in Manila handle visa work beyond the Philippines; close to one million people in Canada claim Filipino ancestry; former ambassador Peter MacArthur, who served in 2020 and 2022, said locally hired Filipino staff are particularly effective, that English is a working language, that the mission does back-office work for other Indo-Pacific embassies, and that it has become a global processing centre for Immigration Canada; and this year Ottawa named Lieutenant-General Derek Macaulay, the Chief of the Defence Staff's envoy to military leaders from Tokyo to Hanoi to Kuala Lumpur, as Canada's first senior military representative for the Indo-Pacific. episodes.content:
# Omni View North America
> **A Wednesday House vote could put Defense Secretary Hegseth on trial in the Senate.**

**What You Need to Know:** A Wednesday House vote could put Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on trial in the Senate. Representative Thomas Massie, a Kentucky Republican, forced that timetable on impeachment articles focused on the Iran war, and President Trump answered by crediting Hegseth with a war in Venezuela and a war still underway in Iran. Approval in the House would send the charges to the Senate.

### Lead
**Thomas Massie Moves to Force Vote on Impeaching Pete Hegseth: The New York Times**
Representative Thomas Massie, a Kentucky Republican, set in motion articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, and The New York Times reported that the House vote must occur by Wednesday. The Washington Post said the effort is focused on the Iran war. The Guardian reported that Massie accuses Hegseth of illegally waging war without congressional authorization. If the House approves the charges, the Times said, a Senate trial follows. President Trump defended Hegseth by saying he “won two wars,” that he “won the war in Venezuela,” and that the United States military raid to capture former president Nicolás Maduro “was flawless.” Trump added that Hegseth is “winning the war in Iran,” and he called Massie “a stone cold loser” and “sick.” Reuters reported that Hegseth is expected to face the House vote this week, and Spectrum News reported that Massie is seeking the vote as incoming members of Congress arrive. Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/09/us/politics/hegseth-impeachment-massie.html) Source: [washingtonpost.com](https://www.washingtonpost.com/national-security/2026/11/09/hegseth-impeachment-effort-begins-house-focused-iran-war/) Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/live/2026/nov/09/donald-trump-stephen-miller-immigration-midterms-iran-qatar-economy-latest-news-updates) Source: [reuters.com](https://www.reuters.com/world/us/hegseth-faces-expected-us-house-impeachment-vote-this-week-2026-11-09/) Source: [spectrumnews1.com](https://spectrumnews1.com/ky/louisville/news/2026/11/09/massie-hegseth-impeachment-congress)

### Across the Region
**What Winnipeg can learn from Toronto’s housing model: Global News**
A mental health and addictions hospital and 2,000 housing units are to be built in Winnipeg on the model of a Toronto project, Global News reported. Prime Minister Mark Carney, at a Friday news conference at Wehwehneh Bahgahkinahgohn, promised to end homelessness across Canada within a decade. The 2026 federal budget sets $1 billion for a Winnipeg Centre for Mental Health and Addictions and for transitional homes. That budget credits Toronto’s Dunn House with a 52 per cent drop in emergency-room visits and more than $2 million in savings. Kinew said the status quo is not working and that standing up 2,000 units and settling people by 2031 means looking everywhere. Doug Rollins, the City of Toronto’s executive director of the housing secretariat, said the units will have rooms, medical offices, and shared spaces such as a kitchen and a community room. Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12143498/what-winnipeg-can-learn-from-torontos-housing-model/)

**US supreme court clears way for Trump’s border wall in Texas’s Big Bend: The Guardian**
The US Supreme Court allowed the Trump administration to resume a border wall in Texas’s Big Bend, including parts of Big Bend National Park, in an unsigned five-page ruling that suspended a lower-court order from last month. Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson was the only dissent. The justices wrote that a 1996 immigration law lets the homeland security secretary waive environmental and conservation requirements, and that Congress’s preference for expeditious border construction outweighs the aesthetic, recreational, and environmental harms claimed by the Center for Biological Diversity, a Big Bend river guide, and a church preservation group. The administration plans more than 300 miles of six-foot vehicle barriers and roads; Customs and Border Protection has awarded five contracts worth more than $6 billion for upgrades that include 30-foot steel fencing, vehicle barriers, and surveillance technology it calls a “smart wall.” Commissioner Rodney Scott said the wall is going up at about 12 miles a week and is expected to be finished by the end of President Trump’s second term. The Center called the ruling a “horrific decision” that lets contractors bulldoze desert and dynamite canyon walls before legality is decided, and it said a CBP map covers remote park canyons with no documented unauthorized vehicle crossings; after a federal judge paused work in October, CBP said it remained confident in its authority “to secure the border while preserving the unique landscape of the Big Bend region.” Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/09/us-supreme-court-border-wall-texas-big-bend) Source: [usatoday.com](https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/nation/2026/11/09/texans-supreme-court-decision-big-bend-border-wall/92698754007/)

### The Closer Look
**US Senate advances New Mexico US Sen. Heinrich’s controversial permit reform bill: Source New Mexico**
On Monday evening the United States Senate voted 73 to 25 to end debate on the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, the permitting bill New Mexico Democrat Martin Heinrich has championed with a bipartisan group of senators. Ending debate took 60 yes votes. The bill now goes to the Senate floor, where senators may add amendments, before a final vote expected in the coming days. It aims to hasten federal environmental reviews of energy projects, and it has drawn criticism from other members of New Mexico’s congressional delegation over provisions they say will weaken environmental protections and exclude tribes from a meaningful role.

Heinrich and his cosponsors released an amended text on Saturday. On Monday morning he and Rhode Island Democrat Sheldon Whitehouse urged senators to pass the bill. Members of the All Pueblo Council of Governors, representing New Mexico Pueblos, flew to Washington that day to urge a no vote. They say the bill, including the Saturday amendment, makes harmful development on sacred sites more likely. Gov.-elect Deb Haaland opposed the amended bill. Attorney General Raúl Torrez opposed it in a letter to Senate leaders signed by attorneys general from several other states. Senator Ben Ray Luján, Democrat of New Mexico, cast one of the no votes. He said he supports faster clean-energy and infrastructure development but, after a month listening to tribal leaders and environmentalists, cannot support advancing the bill in its current form. Other members of Congress said they oppose the bill because they cannot trust President Trump’s administration to permit renewable projects along with fossil-fuel projects such as pipelines.

While the votes were cast, Trump said at a news conference that he fully supported the permitting bill and that he would not approve any new wind turbines, which the bill seeks to encourage. “The bill hasn’t been fully negotiated,” he told reporters, according to The Hill as quoted by Source New Mexico. “I will not approve wind turbines because wind turbines are a major loser.” Heinrich said the bill would reduce energy costs while many Americans are frustrated with rising prices, and would hold data centers financially liable for new costs they impose on energy grids. Erik Schlenker-Goodrich, executive director of the Western Environmental Law Center, said both chambers should wait until January, when a new Democratic majority could have a constructive conversation about renewable infrastructure. He said the sponsors’ urgency exists “to minimize scrutiny and prevent lawmakers and Americans from understanding the enormity of BAAJA’s power transfer away from the people and to the oligarch class.” If the Senate passes the bill, it heads to the House. Source: [sourcenm.com](https://sourcenm.com/2026/11/09/us-senate-advances-new-mexico-us-sen-heinrichs-controversial-permit-reform-bill/) Source: [santafenewmexican.com](https://www.santafenewmexican.com/news/environment/heinrich-s-energy-permitting-reform-bill-passes-senate-procedural-vote/article_6ee3cbcf-282e-4794-867c-0b1ccfdbc1f1.html)

> **Republicans choose Jordan and Thune after the House's biggest defeat in decades, resetting who leads them.**

**What You Need to Know:** Republicans have chosen Jordan and Thune as leaders after the House's biggest election defeat in decades, resetting who leads them in Congress. In the House they signaled a desire for fresh leadership; in the Senate they re-elected their current leader. The New York Times reports both moves.

### Lead
**Stung by Losses, G.O.P. Chooses Jordan and Thune as Leaders: The New York Times**
The New York Times reports that, stung by losses, Republicans chose Jordan and Thune as leaders. In the House, Republicans signaled a desire for fresh leadership after their biggest election defeat in decades. In the Senate, they re-elected their current leader. The House result is a turn in who sets the minority's direction after that defeat. The Senate result is continuity: the current leader stays. Together, the two choices decide who speaks for Republicans in each chamber as the new Congress takes shape. Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/10/us/politics/republican-house-leader-scalise-jordan.html)

### Across the Region
**Carney weighs end to Western Arctic offshore drilling ban ahead of 2028 expiry: The Hub**
Prime Minister Mark Carney is weighing an end to the Western Arctic offshore drilling ban ahead of its 2028 expiry, The Hub reports. He says Ottawa is consulting on the future of the Arctic offshore oil and gas drilling ban, CBC reports. The ban is the restriction now in force on offshore drilling in that part of the Arctic. What is being decided is whether it ends before 2028 or runs to that expiry. The people affected are those with a stake in Arctic offshore oil and gas, and the consultation is the step Carney says is underway. Source: [thehub.ca](https://thehub.ca/2026/11/11/carney-weighs-end-to-western-arctic-offshore-drilling-ban-ahead-of-2028-expiry/) Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/arctic-drilling-consultation-mark-carney-canada-9.7416538)

Critics are crying foul, NPR reports. The convictions are the legal results now being asked to be set aside. What changes, if the dismissals go through, is the standing of those convictions for Bannon and for the Oath Keepers. ### The Closer Look
**Ukrainian war veteran from Manitoba's Interlake walks the walk in fundraising campaign: Yahoo News Canada**
Peter Derksen, 60, a retired Winnipeg police officer from Manitoba's Interlake, has completed a nearly six-month hike of more than 4,000 kilometres on the Pacific Crest Trail, on foot from the U.S.-Mexico border to Canada, to raise money for Ukraine's war effort. He began in early April and reached the northern terminus in late September. On October 5, just over a month after he finished, he said he never doubted he would finish, even though it was a momentous task and incredibly difficult. He said nothing he put up with in his suffering equated to what soldiers are suffering in Ukraine.

The trail begins near Campo, California, and ends at Manning Provincial Park in British Columbia. Hikers who complete it cross 26 national forests and three U.S. states. Derksen averaged the equivalent of a marathon each day, carrying up to 50 pounds of camping gear, food and water. The trail officially spans about 4,265 kilometres; he estimated he walked over 5,000 because of fire closures, rerouting and diversions to restock. He faced the heat of Southern California, an American black bear and her cubs in the Sierra Nevada, and he summited Mount Whitney, the highest peak in the contiguous United States, on his 60th birthday. He witnessed multiple helicopter rescues of other hikers. Chris Rylee, communications director for the Pacific Crest Trail Association, called a single continuous hike an audacious proposal that very few attempt and even fewer complete. The association generally sees about 5,000 permit applications a year and around 1,000 to 2,000 self-reported completions; only a tiny handful are thru-hikers who finish without skipping sections.

The hike left swelling and calluses that grew his feet nearly three shoe sizes, plus stress fractures and numbness in his toes. He calls that numbness Christmas toe: the feeling, hikers say, comes back by Christmas. He raised over $7,000 for two charities, including the Canada-Ukraine Foundation. Valeriy Kostyuk, the foundation's executive director, said the impact goes beyond fundraising to keeping Ukraine relevant, and that the foundation has contributed more than $100 million in aid since the invasion, all of it from donations. Derksen had served about three years with the Royal Winnipeg Rifles reserve and specialized in security, weapons handling and tactical procedures with the Winnipeg Police Service. He travelled to Ukraine in September 2022 and stayed until September 2023, first with the International Legion for the Defence of Ukraine and later as a member of the Ukrainian army. His brigade, he said, operated near the front lines and often suffered multiple casualties each day. Soldiers who fought alongside him have reached out to thank him. He said he kept walking so the world would stay aware that Ukrainians are still struggling to live peacefully and free. Source: [ca.news.yahoo.com](https://ca.news.yahoo.com/ukrainian-war-veteran-manitobas-interlake-100000054.html) Source: [ca.news.yahoo.com](https://ca.news.yahoo.com/ukrainian-war-vet-manitoba-goes-100000387.html)

episodes.content:
# Omni View North America
> **One hundred twenty-eight billion dollars in Crown assets are set to merge to grow Canadian firms abroad.**

**What You Need to Know:** One hundred twenty-eight billion dollars in Crown assets are set to merge to grow Canadian firms abroad. Ottawa’s budget mandate would combine Export Development Canada and the Business Development Bank of Canada. Elsewhere, Ontario is weighing an end to the local veto on new landfills as the province says dump space is running short.

### Lead
**Ottawa mandates a merger of EDC and BDC: The Globe and Mail**
Export Development Canada and the Business Development Bank of Canada, both Crown corporations that finance businesses, are under a mandate to combine, one of the steps Ottawa promised in the federal budget unveiled earlier this month. Together they hold $128-billion in assets, 5,100 employees and a footprint in more than two dozen countries. Alison Nankivell, EDC’s chief executive, said the aim is more Canadian companies of a certain size with a real presence in several markets, and that the combination is not a cost cut but a larger balance sheet that can move resources. Two people with knowledge of the plans told The Globe and Mail the new body will report to the Minister of Finance, part of a wider consolidation of federally backed financing agencies; the Globe is not naming them because they were not authorized to speak publicly. In a September white paper, EDC ranked Canada 35th for the complexity of goods it produces, behind Japan, South Korea, Germany, China, Sweden, Italy, the United States and France, and estimated Canada could add $100-billion to GDP by making more complex products. Nankivell pointed to critical minerals, the energy transition, artificial intelligence, agri-food and forestry, and said ruptures in trade with the United States mean firms can no longer assume supply chains will cross that border without friction; Tushar Handiekar, EDC’s vice-president of structured and project finance, said he expects other countries’ export agencies or insurers to take slices of the lending risk, and Nankivell said the assets overseen should keep growing with the number of firms financed abroad. Source: [theglobeandmail.com](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/business/article-edc-bdc-merger-corporate-champions-global-footprints/)

### Across the Region
**Judge sets a June 2028 trial in the 9/11 case: The New York Times**
A judge has set a June 5, 2028, trial date for four men accused of conspiring in the 2001 attacks that killed nearly 3,000 people. The New York Times reports that years of U.S. government decisions, from coerced confessions to the creation of an alternative court system, doomed prospects for a speedy trial. Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/12/us/politics/torture-9-11.html)

**Kennedy Center plans a switch to Ticketmaster: NPR**
The Kennedy Center plans to switch to Ticketmaster, a move NPR says is raising conflict-of-interest concerns. Former president Richard Grenell was a paid board member of Ticketmaster’s parent company at the same time the two sides were negotiating. Source: [npr.org](https://www.npr.org/2026/11/12/nx-s1-6031461/kennedy-center-ticketmaster-conflict-of-interest)

**Younger Canadians shop retro tech for the holidays: Global News**
A Best Buy Canada survey conducted by Angus Reid finds 40 percent of Canadians likely to buy a holiday gift out of nostalgia, rising to 53 percent of millennials and 49 percent of Gen Z. Kushal Samy, the chain’s director of brand marketing, said younger buyers are rediscovering older formats because they want technology that feels personal, not nostalgia alone. One-third of respondents said they are drawn to old tech because they value owning physical media; 23 percent bought music, movies or games in a physical format in the last year, including 32 percent of millennials, 30 percent of Gen Z and 12 percent of boomers. Gen Z showed the most interest in the Apple iPod, then the Blackberry; millennials favoured consoles such as the Nintendo 64 or Super Nintendo; boomers were most nostalgic for VCRs and VHS. A separate Angus Reid survey released last month found 37 percent of Canadians had cancelled at least one streaming service in the past six months, up from 32 percent four years ago. Best Buy said headphones, earbuds, game consoles and turntables or vinyl are popular categories this year. Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12146554/retro-nostalgia-tech-best-buy/)

### The Closer Look
**Ontario minister open to changes on the landfill veto: The Globe and Mail**
Ontario Environment Minister Todd McCarthy says he is open to changes to his proposal to eliminate a municipal veto on new landfills. He had argued the change is necessary because the province is short of places to put its garbage. Unveiling the plan last month in an omnibus red-tape bill, he said Ontario has less than 10 years of landfill space left. He warned that a new 50-per-cent U.S. tariff imposed by President Donald Trump on trash that crosses the border would make the shortage worse. He said Ontario sends 40 per cent of its commercial waste to Michigan and New York State.

The bill would remove an Environmental Assessment Act section that makes proponents show support from the host municipality and from others within 3.5 kilometres of the site. The same Progressive Conservative government inserted that section in 2020, siding with rural municipalities that opposed taking big-city waste against their will. Ford and his party campaigned in 2018 on a local veto after a proposal for 17.4 million tonnes of waste in a quarry two kilometres from Ingersoll rallied a coalition of 150 municipalities.

McCarthy told The Globe and Mail the deletion would be a housekeeping amendment and that he is open to tweaks. He said that technically the veto is being removed, that this is still a proposal, and that a legislative committee will consider alternatives. Municipalities would keep input and permitting powers, which the province’s land tribunal can override. He expects enough willing communities for new landfills and for energy-from-waste incinerators, a faster process that environmentalists say brings pollution and greenhouse gas emissions.

Late last month he left the door open on forcing a municipality to accept a site; the next day he said no municipality would be forced to accept trash. Last year special legislation let proponents revive and expand a landfill in Dresden while skipping an environmental assessment, over local opposition.

On Nov. 2, 12 Oxford County mayors and mayors-elect warned the changes would leave municipalities without leverage or a meaningful voice and with little chance to negotiate safeguards. Marcus Ryan, outgoing warden and mayor of Zorra Township, said he will meet McCarthy to try to preserve the veto and blamed waste-industry lobbying. He said there is no indication the quarry owners intend to revive their proposal. Bryan Smith, chair of the Oxford Coalition for Social Justice, said the government appears to be talking out of both sides of its mouth. > **Eight people are dead after a Brooklyn collapse, and the search for victims is over.**

**Rescue Ends in Brooklyn After 8 Die in Building Collapse: The New York Times**

Source: [theglobeandmail.com](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/canada/article-flooding-worsens-along-bcs-south-coast-as-heavy-rains-continue/) Source: [npr.org](https://www.npr.org/2026/11/13/nx-s1-6032777/rivers-in-the-sky-are-raining-down-on-the-pacific-northwest-what-are-they)

It is a threat, not a tariff order already in force. Source: [benzinga.com](https://www.benzinga.com/news/politics/26/11/63230809/trump-threatens-to-immediately-double-tariffs-on-mexico-unless-it-stops-migrant-caravans-heading-to-us-there-will-be-no-leniency)

**Howard Lutnick Took Softer Line on Nvidia as Calls for Tougher Controls Grew: The New York Times**
The New York Times reported that President Trump called Nvidia chief Jensen Huang on Tuesday and urged him to fight for his job, continuing what the paper called a pattern of support as a spy scandal intensified. The Times also reported that critics say Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and his department have shielded Nvidia as concerns have grown over A.I. chip sales to firms like Megaspeed, and that Lutnick took a softer line as calls for tougher controls grew. The Guardian reported that Huang resigned on Thursday and was replaced on an interim basis by chief financial officer Colette Kress after reports of affairs, including with Alice Huang, described by that paper as suspected of being a Chinese spy and no relation to him, and that Lutnick faces being fired over an apparent lack of action, including delays in adding MegaSpeed to a trade blacklist. Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/12/us/politics/lutnick-nvidia-commerce-china-chips.html) Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/12/us/politics/trump-jensen-huang-nvidia.html) Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/13/nvidia-scandal-sparks-us-national-security-concerns-china)

### The Closer Look
**Toronto orthodox priest criticized for accepting medal from Putin: Global News**
A Toronto priest accepted a Russian state medal from Vladimir Putin at the Kremlin on November 4, and the Ukrainian Canadian Congress called that choice disgraceful. Global News reported that Putin presented the Order of Friendship to Father Vladimir Malchenko, head priest at Toronto’s Holy Trinity Russian Orthodox Church, during a ceremony on Russia’s National Unity Day. Video the network obtained shows Malchenko walking onto a stage to greet Putin, who shakes his hand and pins the honour onto his frock. Putin commended him for helping Canadian parishioners maintain their connection with their historical homeland, and in the same remarks celebrated Russian troops he said were bravely fighting in Ukraine. Malchenko’s acceptance speech lauded the Fatherland. He said Russians live in all cities and countries but have one Fatherland — Russia, Holy Rus — and asked that God bless it with prosperity and well-being forever.

The Order of Friendship is awarded for outstanding contributions to strengthening friendship and fostering peace and friendly relations among countries. After Russia’s 2022 assault on Kyiv, Canada placed Putin on its Russia sanctions list, citing his grave breach of international peace and security. Kirill, patriarch of the Russian Orthodox Church, whom Global News described as a cheerleader of the attack and who has called it a holy war, was also sanctioned. Global News reported that the International Criminal Court wants Putin for war crimes for the abduction of Ukrainian children. Former prime minister Jean Chrétien received the same order before Putin sent troops into Ukraine in 2014.

Reached by phone after returning to Toronto, Malchenko said he had no regrets. He told Global News he did not see the medal as a political act but as recognition of pastoral duties in Canada, and that his community was grateful for recognition of work to comfort people’s lives there. He said the church was above politics, did not support any wars, and was greatly concerned about human suffering caused by armed conflicts. He said he did not raise the war in Ukraine with Putin because it was not time for a conversation, and that the church never talks about the war.

The Ukrainian Canadian Congress took the opposite view. Chief executive Danylo Korbabicz called the acceptance disgraceful and a textbook case of moral hypocrisy unbecoming of someone who purports to promote Christian teaching. Two days before the ceremony, Russia bombed a school in Ukraine’s Zaporizhzhia region that was used as a humanitarian hub, killing more than 50 people. The night before that attack, a hospital complex was struck, injuring at least 73, and the bombing of a hospice in Dnipro forced the evacuation of dozens of terminally ill and elderly patients. On Wednesday, Canada joined G7 allies in condemning attacks on residential buildings, civilian infrastructure, and cultural heritage. Global Affairs Canada did not respond to requests for comment.

The church’s website links to Russian online platforms that claim Ukraine is an imaginary country and that Ukrainians are imaginary people, language Global News said lines up with propaganda used to justify the military campaign. The church is a registered charity that receives government tax breaks. In 2012, the Conservative government awarded Malchenko the Queen’s Diamond Jubilee Medal. Putin, using his term special military operation, said fighters were defending Russia’s interests and statehood, and he pointed to past wars he said drove invaders from what he called Russia’s native lands. Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12145277/toronto-orthodox-priest-criticized-for-accepting-medal-from-putin/)

episodes.episode_title: Ep 47: Thousands of US passengers were stranded Friday when failing routers halted every takeoff.
episodes.content:
# Omni View North America

> **Thousands of US passengers were stranded Friday when failing routers halted every takeoff.**

The New York Times put the stranded at thousands while NPR said millions, and Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin split on whether old hardware or newer gear caused the failure. Prime Minister Mark Carney, in Manila, said Canada had finished free-trade talks with the Philippines and was not yet at a US deal he would accept for the auto sector.

### Lead
**What to Know About Friday’s Nationwide Ground Stop: The New York Times**
The Federal Aviation Administration issued a rare nationwide ground stop Friday afternoon after outdated air-traffic communications equipment became overloaded with data and began to fail, The New York Times reported, with NPR also covering the halt. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said at the White House that night that radar and other communications started to falter at 3:36 p.m. when old routers overloaded, pervasive enough to stop takeoffs even though the failures were not universal. The Times said the outage stranded thousands and left airlines and airports still recovering; NPR said millions of passengers were stranded and that no planes were taking off at any airport. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said there was zero evidence of a cyberattack and suggested new equipment and new technology Duffy’s department had added to the old infrastructure had overwhelmed it, while Duffy insisted the cause was antiquated legacy communications equipment, not recent upgrades. In a separate account Mullin called the stop a telecommunication outage and said he did not know the cause; speaking at the White House briefing NPR attended, he said there was not a threat to the United States. Duffy said that during the intermittent outage controllers could still reach pilots. Radio transmissions had a Newark Liberty controller sharing the stop with pilots, then Atlanta and Chicago controllers saying they had limited information, then talk of significant gate trouble and a tarmac compared to a parking lot; one pilot told a Newark controller it was not lost on him that it was Friday the 13th. Administration officials demanded that lawmakers approve tens of billions of dollars more to accelerate systemwide upgrades. The last nationwide ground stop, in 2023, came after a pilot warning system went down and lasted around 90 minutes. Travelers whose flights were canceled are entitled to refunds regardless of the reason, though airlines will not guarantee a hotel room or meal vouchers. Some professional and college sports teams were stuck on runways or turning to buses ahead of weekend games now uncertain, and airports filled with stuck families and stranded travelers; passengers on tarmacs told NPR they were stuck without information. In Denver, where Democrats had gathered for a conference after midterm wins, former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg stood at a hotel bar as CNN carried the administration news conference and told a Times reporter he had questions, offering comic-book swearing characters in place of a printable reaction. At a table sat Governors Abigail Spanberger of Virginia and Mikie Sherrill of New Jersey and Senator Elissa Slotkin of Michigan, eating Parmesan fries and checking phones; Senator Raphael Warnock of Georgia scanned Senate group chats for updates from secure channels and from Senator Mark Warner of Virginia. A New England operative booked a rental car for Boston; others looked up Amtrak and found the East Coast more than 40 hours away; aides to a Democratic governor who had arrived on a private jet fielded hitch-a-ride questions. Anne Caprara, chief of staff to Illinois Governor JB Pritzker, who was not in Denver, worked two phones and said Pritzker was furious about the lack of information from the Trump administration, calling the bar Denver’s hottest and likening it to the Mos Eisley Cantina, with a Veep cast and a Terminator 2 mood. Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/13/us/faa-ground-stop-flights-what-to-know.html) Source: [npr.org](https://www.npr.org/2026/11/13/nx-s1-6040388/what-we-know-about-the-faa-nationwide-ground-stop) Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/13/us/ground-stop-air-traffic-control-pilots.html) Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/13/us/faa-ground-stop-outage-plane-landings.html) Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/13/us/ground-stop-flight-delays-cancellations-tips.html) Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/13/us/2023-ground-stop-faa-pilot-warning-system.html) Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/13/us/markwayne-mullin-faa-ground-stop.html) Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/13/us/ground-stop-flights-democrats-denver.html) Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/13/us/ground-stop-flights-sports-nba-football.html) Source: [npr.org](https://www.npr.org/2026/11/13/nx-s1-6040418/dhs-head-markwayne-mullin-says-there-is-not-a-threat-to-the-u-s-amid-faa-ground-stop) Source: [npr.org](https://www.npr.org/2026/11/13/nx-s1-6040397/stuck-on-the-tarmac-without-information-travelers-share-their-ground-stop-experiences) Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/13/us/airports-stranded-travelers.html)

### Across the Region
**Canada making progress in USMCA talks to ensure long-term viability of auto sector, Carney says: The Globe and Mail**
Speaking to reporters in Manila, where he announced Canada had wrapped up talks on a trade agreement with the Philippines, Prime Minister Mark Carney said Canada is making headway with the United States on terms that would leave a path to profitability for Canadian auto production, The Globe and Mail reported, and UA.NEWS carried his statement that the Philippines talks had concluded. He called talks over autos one of the most challenging issues in the negotiations with Washington, said he will not accept a US deal that would kill the Canadian auto sector, and said this government will not settle for a deal that is not consistent with a viable Canadian auto sector. He said he had a long, substantive conversation with President Donald Trump just before leaving on a trip that has taken him from Dublin to Asia for three summits, with White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller and US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer among those on the call. He said he sees a one-on-one deal with the United States to scale back the US tariffs that currently cover steel, aluminum and autos, and that there is the possibility of a bilateral deal but Canada is not yet there. He said the sustainability of the auto industry, premised on continued market access to the United States, is non-negotiable, and that Canada is making gains on auto terms in part because longer-term competitiveness of the US auto sector depends on factors that include the degree of integration with the Canadian sector. He said the North American industry as a whole faces significant competitive challenges because of the speed of change and the shift to electric vehicles, and that this will require big investment. A 25 percent US tariff on Canadian-made autos, minus a carve-out for US parts in the vehicles, has put severe pressure on an industry that typically exports nearly 90 percent of production to the United States; the value of Canadian passenger car and light truck exports to the US tumbled nearly 12 percent from 2024 to 2025, and exports are tracking even lower in 2026. In August, Washington offered to lower the headline tariff rate to 15 percent as part of a broader trade deal that would have reduced Section 232 duties on several key Canadian industries in return for concessions from Ottawa; the US parts carve-out would have been maintained, but the relief would not have been extended to medium- and heavy-duty trucks. Many in the Canadian auto industry balked at that proposal and applauded Carney’s decision to walk away, a choice the Globe said has left an unsustainable status quo. Stellantis is trying to sell its idled Brampton, Ontario, plant to armoured-vehicle manufacturer Roshel. Industry Minister Mélanie Joly said Friday that Ottawa, the Ontario government and the union representing workers at the plant have put an aggressive package in front of Stellantis and remain in solution mode to prevent the sale; Carney declined to offer details of the package and said the details and implications will come out in due course. Source: [theglobeandmail.com](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/politics/article-canada-making-progress-in-usmca-talks-to-ensure-long-term-viability-of/) Source: [ua.news](https://ua.news/en/dovkolo-svitu/karni-zaiaviv-pro-zavershennia-peregovoriv-kanadi-z-filippinami-channel-newsasia)

**Trump Administration Delays Enforcement of Medicaid Work Requirement: The New York Times**
The federal government had planned to require poor adults to prove they were working or lose insurance coverage starting January 1. It will now let states wait until July. The change pushes back the date those adults can lose coverage for failing to document work, from the first day of the year to midsummer, and it is a delay in enforcement rather than a repeal of the requirement itself. Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/13/us/politics/medicaid-work-requirement-delay.html)

**Alaska Senate Race Between Dan Sullivan and Mary Peltola Still Counting Votes: The New York Times**
In the only Senate race still uncalled, Democrat Mary Peltola widened her lead over Republican Senator Dan Sullivan in Alaska’s latest tally, The New York Times reported Friday night. She had 49.8 percent of the vote and led Sullivan by nearly four percentage points in incomplete results as of Friday night. If neither candidate wins an outright majority, the race will be decided next week by ranked-choice tabulation. A New York Times analysis said she is on track to eventually prevail; Sullivan spokesman Nate Adams said Friday night, after the latest release of results, that the campaign is still waiting for every ballot to be counted and will see what happens from there. The delay is in part because of the time Alaska allows for mail ballots to be received and counted and in part because of the state’s ranked-choice system. Sullivan, a two-term incumbent, and Peltola, a former congresswoman, faced two other candidates after emerging from a nonpartisan primary in August. The contest sits inside a midterm cycle the Times described as featuring sweeping Democratic victories, and it remains the only Senate battle still uncalled. Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/14/us/alaska-senate-race-ranked-choice-tabulation.html)

**Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins wins race for Alaska governor, replaces a Republican: NPR**
Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins, a former state legislator who campaigned on bipartisanship in a state that usually votes Republican, won Alaska’s governor race, replaces a Republican, and at 37 will be the youngest governor in the state’s history, NPR reported. episodes.episode_title: Ep 48: Black women will hold seven of Georgia's top eight elected leadership posts, all of them…
episodes.content:
# Omni View North America
> **Black women will hold seven of Georgia's top eight elected leadership posts, all of them Democrats.**

**What You Need to Know:** Black women, all Democrats, will hold seven of the top eight elected leadership roles in Georgia, The New York Times reports, after offices long held by Republican men changed hands up and down the ballot. Mary-Pat Hector, 28, told the Times she and a veteran organizer cried on the phone once a result they had treated as someday work arrived in one night, including her hope that Keisha Lance Bottoms would make Georgia the first state to elect a Black woman as governor. The Times describes that shift as the product of decades of door-knocking, registration and rides to the polls by Black women in a state that had been under Republican control.

### Lead
**The Reward for Black Women's Work in Georgia: Leaders Who Look Like Them: The New York Times**
The New York Times reports that Black women, all Democrats, will hold seven of the top eight elected leadership roles in Georgia. Mary-Pat Hector, 28, volunteered on Election Day to help get dozens of voters to the polls after months spent trying to energize other young people behind Democratic candidates. The Times calls her a Gen Z torchbearer for organizing traditions handed down over generations of Black women, and says she was prepared for a good night. She was hopeful that Keisha Lance Bottoms would win, which would make Georgia the first state to elect a Black woman as governor. The Times reports that history kept being made after that hope: up and down the ballot, Black women, all Democrats, claimed positions that had long been occupied by Republican men. Hector called a mentor, a veteran organizer in the state; both women were stunned, and a future they had thought might be attainable someday was suddenly materializing. "We both just cried on the phone," Hector said, "because we have been doing this work for so long." She added that they could at last "see the fruits of our labor." The Times describes Black women as, for decades, a trusted base and the most relied-upon foot soldiers for Democrats in Georgia: knocking on doors, registering friends and neighbors, driving strangers to the polls, and coaxing people who had all but written off the government to show up anyway. That incremental work, the Times writes, revived Democratic fortunes in the state after years of Republican control. Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/15/us/black-women-georgia-leaders.html)

### Across the Region
**Fifth Canadian soldier dies following military base fire: A News**
Private William Douglas Dal Bianco, of the 3rd Battalion, Princess Patricia's Canadian Light Infantry, died Friday in Ontario from injuries sustained in an October fire at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright. Prime Minister Mark Carney announced the death on Saturday. A News, CBC and The Globe and Mail all identify him as the fifth Canadian soldier to die of injuries from that fire. The toll from the Wainwright fire now stands at five members of the Canadian military, with Dal Bianco's death the latest, not a new blaze. Source: [anews.com.tr](https://www.anews.com.tr/world/2026/11/15/fifth-canadian-soldier-dies-following-military-base-fire) Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/edmonton/fifth-soldier-dies-cfb-wainwright-fire-9.7422365) Source: [theglobeandmail.com](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/canada/article-fifth-soldier-dead-cfb-wainwright-fire-october/)

**Midterm voters ended the long-running GOP dominance in state legislatures: NPR**
NPR reports that midterm voters ended long-running Republican dominance in state legislatures. In several states, Democrats took control of legislatures that had been divided, and they weakened Republican dominance in others. NPR says issues on the agenda in those chambers include more access to health care and new limits on school vouchers. The shift is a result of the midterm vote, not a proposal still awaiting an election. Source: [npr.org](https://www.npr.org/2026/11/15/nx-s1-6039175/midterms-legislatures-states-democrats-gop)

**Two Planes Collide on a Taxiway at Miami International Airport: The New York Times**
The wingtip of a Copa Airlines Boeing 737 struck the nose of a UPS Boeing 767 on a taxiway at Miami International Airport around 9 p.m. Saturday, the Federal Aviation Administration said. The Copa plane was taxiing to the gate after arriving from Panama City; the UPS plane was taxiing for departure to Bogotá, Colombia, and air traffic controllers had told the UPS crew to give way to the Copa flight. Greg Chin, a spokesman for the Miami-Dade Aviation Department, said the planes made contact at the intersection of two taxiways. Two people were treated at the scene for minor injuries, and flights were routed to other taxiways without disrupting airport operations, Chin said. The FAA is investigating. The collision came a day after a nationwide ground stop disrupted air travel, and just over two months after an Amazon cargo jet overran a runway at the same airport, struck two vehicles and killed five people; a federal report found an air-traffic controller had failed to warn those pilots about windy conditions when giving them permission to land. Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/15/us/miami-airport-plane-collision-copa-ups.html)

### Also Today
**How Pennsylvania Democrats flipped the Senate and won a trifecta: PhillyBurbs**
PhillyBurbs reports that Pennsylvania Democrats flipped the state Senate and won a trifecta. Source: [buckscountycouriertimes.com](https://www.buckscountycouriertimes.com/story/news/politics/elections/state/2026/11/15/pennsylvania-democrats-senate-trifecta-2026/92756948007/)

A bomb discovered Friday afternoon at the BioUrja Renewables plant in Peoria, Illinois, forced evacuations; officials say it has been rendered safe but called it a credible threat, and the FBI is investigating.
